In endorsing the Democratic candidate, Amy Actin, The Plain Dealer said, "And Ramaswamy's decision to release this vile advertisement reveals a failure of judgment that Ohio cannot afford in its governor." | == \- WFSA12 The State of Alabama has released the final version of the Ten Commandments poster for every public school classroom in the state. | A CALL TO ACTION | This won't be a year when we can sit back and expect everyone else to do the work. If you want to change the direction of the country, you have to get into the game. If you can help us with any of these efforts, drop us a note, and we will be in touch. Here is what you can do to help us win in November: | Make a plan to vote: Tell everyone you know to vote, offer rides to the polls, THEN VOTE. | Sign Waving: Gather some friends and wave signs on any busy streetcorner, we can get you more signs and t-shirts. | | | Events: We're a grassroots campaign, so we need to meet people face-to-face. If you're having a fall festival, food truck event, flea market, farmers market, or art fair, let us know. | | | Canvassing: We need volunteers to help organize canvassing or work with other candidates to coordinate efforts. We can provide lists of addresses for potential swing voters and as many push cards as you want. | | | Phone banking: If your county already does phone banking, we can team with you to include our campaign in your message. | | | Host an event: We want to meet your friends. | | One Last Thought Until Next Week | | | Hey everybody, To quote the late Robert Hunter of The Grateful Dead, "What a long strange trip it's been." We started driving through these eleven counties in the second half of June 2025. Fifteen months and 35,000 miles later, we're down to the end, and in the last few weeks have felt like we have been closing the circle. The first county Democratic party we visited was with the Randolph County Blues. We visited them for the third time two weeks ago. This time, instead of me asking a lot of questions to learn what the county needed or giving a speech about how we were going to help the county, we got to sit and chat with people who have become friends. Our first big public event was in October 2025 at Fall on Main in Roanoke. We went back this weekend, and the vibe had shifted. Last year, the election was more than a year away, and overseas farm markets collapsed because of tariffs, so people had more pressing concerns. This year, only one person refused to talk to me, and he was very polite. Hundreds of people stopped to talk about the election and to hear what we're saying about the issues. Lots of people said they had seen me online, and they were voting for me, and more than a few stopped by to say they had already voted absentee for me. Then on Thursday, we're heading back to Heflin for a Cleburne County Democratic Party meeting. I went to the Cleburne County party in the summer of 2025. We've been there a few times in the last 15 months, and it will be our last county meeting before the election. The one stop I wanted to make but couldn't was in Tallapoosa County. Tallapoosa has been so supportive of this campaign over the last year, and I really wanted to make their candidates' forum, but I felt I needed to close the circle and go back to Fall on Main. I had nothing to worry about. Barb represented the campaign, and everyone said she knocked it out of the park. I'll be honest: I'm exhausted, but looking back over the last 15 months, I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished. Next week, after the votes are counted, I'll write something to tell you all what this means to me. But right now, it is unbelievable that I get to say... We are 7 days away from the general election. Be well. ## 3 Governor Candidates Debate at MTSU

A Scarborough woman says a videographer told her she would be appearing in an ad for Sen. Susan Collins, so she was surprised to see her face appearing in campaign advertisements from Graham Platner's replacement, Troy Jackson.
Kelly Kusnirak, a longtime Republican who owns a laundromat business in the Scarborough area, says footage she recorded last spring for what she believed was a Collins campaign video is now being used in a digital and streaming ad supporting the Democratic challenger.

According to Kusnirak, a videographer approached her at her business around March or April, identified himself as shooting for the Susan Collins campaign, and asked if she would participate. She agreed.
At the time, Jackson had not yet replaced Democratic nominee Graham Platner, who removed himself from the ticket amid allegations of sexual assault. The Maine Democrats concocted a small convention of insiders to fill the vacancy, and Jackson handily secured the several hundred votes it took to become the nominee.
But long before Platner faced sexual assault allegations, and before the world knew that Jackson had fathered two children with his second cousin, a Democrat Party videographer duped Kusnirak into filming what would become a kind of "deep fake" endorsement for Collins' opponent.
"I said yes because I support Susan," Kusnirak said in a statement and in a follow-up video provided to _The Robinson Report_. "I had no idea that months later my face and my words would show up in an ad for her opponent. I feel like I was duped."
In the original short ad, which carries a disclaimer that it was "Paid for by CFFE PAC" and "Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee," Kusnirak sits at a table in front of Speed Queen washers and dryers. On-screen text identifies her as "Kelly, South Portland, ME." She says: "As far as affordability in Maine, nothing is affordable in Maine. Rent is not affordable. Buying a house is not affordable. But do our wages go up? Do we have good jobs in Maine? No."
Kusnirak is never asked whether she thinks the state government, where Jackson has been a top Democratic lawmaker and six-year Senate President, has had anything to do with the cost of housing and stifled wage growth. Or... if she was, that video was left on the cutting room floor.
An overlay attributed to Center for American Progress Action states that "Costs are going up for almost everything Maine families need, and Sen. Susan Collins is making things worse." The ad then cuts to Jackson at a podium with the message: "Susan Collins is too expensive for Maine. Vote Troy Jackson for Senate in November." The website listed is familyfriendlyeconomy.org.

CFFE PAC, the Campaign for a Family Friendly Economy, is a progressive group that focuses on issues such as higher taxes and more government intervention in the economy. It has spent hundreds of thousands of dollars in independent expenditures supporting Jackson in the Maine Senate race.
The PAC's executive director is Sondra Goldschein, a former director at the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU). The group is funded, in part, by Melinda Gates' Pivotal Ventures, and multiple funds controlled by Arabella Advisors and the George Soros network. The PAC has spent nearly $2 million boosting Jackson, but it's not clear how much of that spending went to tricking Collins voters into filming pro-Jackson ads.
Kusnirak says she only learned her footage had been used when a friend saw the ad. In a longer response video filmed in the same laundromat and ending with the "Susan Collins - our senator" branding and a "Paid for by Collins for Senator" disclaimer, she states she is "not a Troy Jackson supporter at all."
"I definitely feel like I was misled because when I did finally see the ad, I was like, oh wow, look at that banner, Troy Jackson," she says. "I was surprised to see that it was for Troy Jackson. Totally did not expect that. I thought it was going to be for Susan Collins."

She continues: "If they're willing to mislead me, how far will they go? And, you know, when will it end?"
In the same video, Kusnirak attributes Maine's affordability problems to state-level decisions rather than Collins: "The economic problems we have in Maine right now are pretty much the result of our legislature in Augusta that has been in control for the past eight years." She adds that Collins "always puts Maine first when she makes decisions that affect Maine and she does more for Mainers economically on certain issues than the legislature in Augusta has done."
Jackson served as President of the Maine Senate during part of the period Kusnirak references. The 2026 contest between the five-term Republican incumbent and the former state Senate leader has been marked by heavy independent expenditures and a focus on cost-of-living issues from both sides.
Kusnirak said she is speaking out so other Mainers are not misled the same way.
"If they're willing to trick me into being in one of his ads, they're willing to trick you into voting for Troy Jackson," she said. "These are dirty tricks, and I think Mainers deserve better. I want to set the record straight: I am voting for Susan Collins."

# Watch the Congressional Debate
Thursday, October 29
7 PM on News 8
Virginia McIntyre and Joe Morelle Dear Neighbor, In this election, you have the unique opportunity to send a message to Washington and make change through the simple act of casting your vote. The political universe is convinced that money decides the winners and losers in elections, which is why our representatives spend more time meeting with donors than meeting us to hear our concerns. **Prove them wrong. Prove to them that the people control our government and that the community has more power than the big donors.** Show them that big political endorsements from governors or presidents mean nothing because, in America, our leaders serve the people and not the other way around. I’m asking for your help to truly continue the legacy that Louise left behind—a legacy of fighting for the people of this district whether they agreed with her or not, and showing up day after day to earn their respect and appreciation no matter what party they belonged to. **Give me a chance to fight for you in Washington—I promise I won’t let you down.**
[ ](https://52zrz7fk.r.us-east-1.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Ftracking.virginiamcintyreforcongress.com%2F%-482ef95f-96ad-47a6-bb2e-9a84fab19659-000000/HLiMzYq5OK4aFNjxGO8G37UG9Wc=473)
Thank you for taking the time to tune in tonight. I am so very grateful. God bless you all, and may God forever bless the United States of America. Sincerely,
**Virginia McIntyre**
Candidate for Congress, NY-25

subject: They're getting doors slammed in their faces
body:
Two weeks until Election Day. Our student canvassers need to know you have their backs.

*|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | |
---
| | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L2uGyEQxfGnYTuvYFjjS0ERyXJ306ZcjWEWo8uXYOwobx85Sl4g9V86-un8-Nw_MeVU43cs5AYf-5g7P-jXoEjMqcbQ2pgzYykUdpBgTkqewO7oOb1o33AJLviAyi_k1MVqMPZDm-XhTLhoOO5nCvKM5gxmC5KUxoPobsOGS3LvPSXBKqkl2BW8UdJ6_NAmyLBpsUnMNHgd1J_3nDxWxvl1tOFp9a0s2T2Y-xT6m4CbgNsk_xy0Tn4GqjyPNnI66E1tdW0jCrh1PHkc1NF_YSQwQt_m8EJfqfQhwJQZUxD6-oYp21GAeXLZPZaOKdZ3-Yv-V1plqiz0dfCxDBf6z5RzmuYiNhkLpvyHyv_57svB7wAAAP__V4KLwg)

Dear Pro-Life Friend,

Our volunteer student canvassers have been through the wringer these past couple of months.

Doors get slammed in their faces. They get shouted off stoops. And sometimes, even worse things happen.

So, I’ve told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two weeks.

Pro-Life Friend, our student canvassers know what’s on the line.

They know if abortion-loving leftists seize power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies.

And they know the job’s not done yet.

But right now, they could use a little moral boost heading into the final weeks before Election Day on Tuesday, November 3rd.

[That’s why I’m hoping you’ll prayerfully consider sending a Care Package to one of our door-to-door canvassers](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L2uGyEQxfGnYTuvYFjjS0ERyXJ306ZcjWEWo8uXYOwobx85Sl4g9V86-un8-Nw_MeVU43cs5AYf-5g7P-jXoEjMqcbQ2pgzYykUdpBgTkqewO7oOb1o33AJLviAyi_k1MVqMPZDm-XhTLhoOO5nCvKM5gxmC5KUxoPobsOGS3LvPSXBKqkl2BW8UdJ6_NAmyLBpsUnMNHgd1J_3nDxWxvl1tOFp9a0s2T2Y-xT6m4CbgNsk_xy0Tn4GqjyPNnI66E1tdW0jCrh1PHkc1NF_YSQwQt_m8EJfqfQhwJQZUxD6-oYp21GAeXLZPZaOKdZ3-Yv-V1plqiz0dfCxDBf6z5RzmuYiNhkLpvyHyv_57svB7wAAAP__V4KLwg)**.**

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

These young women and men will be on their feet for hours, walking door to door. And knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going.

Of course, I could tell our door knockers to go home.

I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead.

But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad ever could. And the effect doesn’t disappear after one election.

**Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote again in the next election, too.**

And, it costs us less than $3 for every door we knock.

This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that’s needed to turn out every pro-life voter.

Last cycle, this approach worked.
**> >> In Oklahoma,** our canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion state senators who killed our legislation to stop chemical abortion pill trafficking. Voters threw them out.

**> >> In South Carolina,** we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who killed our “Life at Conception Act.” They lost too.

**> >> In North Carolina,** 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries.
The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to give up and go home during this final stretch.

It’s true they have the money, the media, and the institutions.

But what they don’t have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger’s door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words, and still go knock on the next door.

That grit and determination is what wins elections.

[So, will you please make your most generous contribution today to keep our canvassers in the field through the two most important weeks of this election season](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L2uGyEQxfGnYTuvYFjjS0ERyXJ306ZcjWEWo8uXYOwobx85Sl4g9V86-un8-Nw_MeVU43cs5AYf-5g7P-jXoEjMqcbQ2pgzYykUdpBgTkqewO7oOb1o33AJLviAyi_k1MVqMPZDm-XhTLhoOO5nCvKM5gxmC5KUxoPobsOGS3LvPSXBKqkl2BW8UdJ6_NAmyLBpsUnMNHgd1J_3nDxWxvl1tOFp9a0s2T2Y-xT6m4CbgNsk_xy0Tn4GqjyPNnI66E1tdW0jCrh1PHkc1NF_YSQwQt_m8EJfqfQhwJQZUxD6-oYp21GAeXLZPZaOKdZ3-Yv-V1plqiz0dfCxDBf6z5RzmuYiNhkLpvyHyv_57svB7wAAAP__V4KLwg)**?**
**> >> $250** fully funds a canvasser’s entire day in the field: more than 80 doors knocked, one voter conversation at a time.

**> >> $100** puts a canvasser on more than 30 doors in a key race.

**> >> $50** covers a tank of gas for a canvasser’s day of driving to and from strategic locations.

**> >> $25** pays for a canvasser’s meals for a day in the field.

**> >> $10** puts our pro-life message on more than three doors.
Pro-Life Friend, door knocking has been our key to beating both the Abortion Lobby and the D.C. consultant class for years.

You see, they like wasting their donors’ money on flashy, expensive cable TV ads because it lines their pockets.

Meanwhile, real people having real conversations are what actually move voters in November. That’s how we helped 119 pro-life legislators WIN in 2024!

So, please let our dedicated student activists know you care about them and appreciate the hard work they’re doing for the entire pro-life movement.

[Will you please send a Care Package to one of our canvassers right now](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L2uGyEQxfGnYTuvYFjjS0ERyXJ306ZcjWEWo8uXYOwobx85Sl4g9V86-un8-Nw_MeVU43cs5AYf-5g7P-jXoEjMqcbQ2pgzYykUdpBgTkqewO7oOb1o33AJLviAyi_k1MVqMPZDm-XhTLhoOO5nCvKM5gxmC5KUxoPobsOGS3LvPSXBKqkl2BW8UdJ6_NAmyLBpsUnMNHgd1J_3nDxWxvl1tOFp9a0s2T2Y-xT6m4CbgNsk_xy0Tn4GqjyPNnI66E1tdW0jCrh1PHkc1NF_YSQwQt_m8EJfqfQhwJQZUxD6-oYp21GAeXLZPZaOKdZ3-Yv-V1plqiz0dfCxDBf6z5RzmuYiNhkLpvyHyv_57svB7wAAAP__V4KLwg)**?**

For Life,

Kristan Hawkins
President, Students for Life Action

P.S. – Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd, and our canvassers will be knocking on doors right up to the finish line. [Please help keep them in the field with a Care Package Gift of $25 or more today](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L2uGyEQxfGnYTuvYFjjS0ERyXJ306ZcjWEWo8uXYOwobx85Sl4g9V86-un8-Nw_MeVU43cs5AYf-5g7P-jXoEjMqcbQ2pgzYykUdpBgTkqewO7oOb1o33AJLviAyi_k1MVqMPZDm-XhTLhoOO5nCvKM5gxmC5KUxoPobsOGS3LvPSXBKqkl2BW8UdJ6_NAmyLBpsUnMNHgd1J_3nDxWxvl1tOFp9a0s2T2Y-xT6m4CbgNsk_xy0Tn4GqjyPNnI66E1tdW0jCrh1PHkc1NF_YSQwQt_m8EJfqfQhwJQZUxD6-oYp21GAeXLZPZaOKdZ3-Yv-V1plqiz0dfCxDBf6z5RzmuYiNhkLpvyHyv_57svB7wAAAP__V4KLwg)**.** _Students for Life Action is a non-profit, tax-exempt advocacy organization under section 501(c)(4) of the IRC. clean_body: Two weeks until Election Day. Our student canvassers need to know you have their backs. |MCPREVIEWTEXT| | | | | | Dear Pro-Life Friend, Our volunteer student canvassers have been through the wringer these past couple of months. Doors get slammed in their faces. They get shouted off stoops. And sometimes, even worse things happen. So, I’ve told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two weeks. Pro-Life Friend, our student canvassers know what’s on the line. They know if abortion-loving leftists seize power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies. And they know the job’s not done yet. But right now, they could use a little moral boost heading into the final weeks before Election Day on Tuesday, November 3rd. . My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement. These young women and men will be on their feet for hours, walking door to door. And knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going. Of course, I could tell our door knockers to go home. I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead. But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad ever could. And the effect doesn’t disappear after one election. Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote again in the next election, too. And, it costs us less than $3 for every door we knock. This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that’s needed to turn out every pro-life voter. Last cycle, this approach worked. >> In Oklahoma, our canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion state senators who killed our legislation to stop chemical abortion pill trafficking. Voters threw them out. >> In South Carolina, we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who killed our “Life at Conception Act.” They lost too. >> In North Carolina, 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries. The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to give up and go home during this final stretch. It’s true they have the money, the media, and the institutions. But what they don’t have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger’s door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words, and still go knock on the next door. That grit and determination is what wins elections. ? >> $250 fully funds a canvasser’s entire day in the field: more than 80 doors knocked, one voter conversation at a time. >> $100 puts a canvasser on more than 30 doors in a key race. >> $50 covers a tank of gas for a canvasser’s day of driving to and from strategic locations. >> $25 pays for a canvasser’s meals for a day in the field. >> $10 puts our pro-life message on more than three doors. Pro-Life Friend, door knocking has been our key to beating both the Abortion Lobby and the D.C. consultant class for years. You see, they like wasting their donors’ money on flashy, expensive cable TV ads because it lines their pockets. Meanwhile, real people having real conversations are what actually move voters in November. That’s how we helped 119 pro-life legislators WIN in 2024! So, please let our dedicated student activists know you care about them and appreciate the hard work they’re doing for the entire pro-life movement. ? For Life, Kristan Hawkins President, Students for Life Action P.S. – Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd, and our canvassers will be knocking on doors right up to the finish line. . ## Brewers Win Team's First World Series
The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 Wednesday night to become [baseball's world champions](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQBuCngc3R-TCQGzx0yZauHZHBZ7jKQGRbQXn7irRv0PF00q__-7_uw91JlG3-dCvbEvZh4yNHLoXTMCY-OOVDtmNP0WdOwnmReRkQsFMaFNLgpiJPHnTtbWBGbmq2uqcGOyLT1IsNDOPVI2gf0IUrOW8MABkkB853oRZ7xmlA0tAg4gVb59H0xIBNB_1YGWAvZU-X7122snCIr_3J6TLtax3tUsojV81HhbcKb-5xCs7XeaQiU-QKb38WldwrqzdH_XrU7FZWraJeBwrjdXK-b8FgmPpApMl70pNuqU7WPw6JUXLXVwbm1Ul8Nyj_2-1p8ScAAP__VA6BUA) for the first time in the franchise's history. Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings of two-hit ball and rookie Cooper Pratt got two hits and two RBIs, bringing down the curtain on one of the most dominant performances in recent postseason baseball. Milwaukee swept the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers in four games to win the National League pennant, and rolled over the Rays in five games, finishing the season with [the second-lowest team ERA](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGnwRsWHI4dBoYu3tK1o4XNOVyFIQIUlLevnPYNuv91p9_3dVtulgLF-6c90NQ9LRFbCVgr5mXN2DCXRrGlHFzBTFg83f0CAkYuBQe92K3SExfZObMjAqoOjZy0glHrQXXerIMdNFi3TRd91RclrlpLlM5ZCU7soiNznpMCtBQKAHq4WAfDpFGAGsW0skGgo5py_50oVo97eKUn5n5LRxeMr_VRmPpgMDOYW2v9tpbySLmWs2AwH2FlMJ-yM_Av_ifjm428UeQ75VL5W8l_mQzmLhv3aBQClXFig7gflsL7Z_3fUk8DPwEAAP__5Nx-lA) in baseball, and leading the majors in batting average and on-base percentage. The team had gone 57 seasons without a championship. Tampa Bay, the American League's best team this season, is now 0-3 in World Series appearances after 2008 and 2020.
## 68 Dead as Spanish Bullet Trains Collide
A high-speed train plowed into the back of a stopped train in central Spain yesterday morning, [killing at least 68](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuxCAQRL_G7nxaLxwcBUWa6y5tSmsNy3kjzrYAnZW_j5xfSPk00ozmfT2mB0mW9flJL_YtbdPKR83cGpdpLnxwqYesx1ZyrFyE6yLPZUJAM4wwoJsoNHnzNPbRJ2Zk1bMfrVNonNOqX3zSClJEduhmBWMImpKdFRNFoACmF3_WjYBuBIWIF7xSRG0dAyoDdu40cJS2lcv3JmtbOOWf7c3lErZXn_3S2l479dHhvcM77eeDMzqhNAmZO7y3QrIOFIJEXttQ9xN1MldtRwJWJml9i5bZcWKw5haitX3xcT8kZ6nGdhqeL5L8t9r-5-rt8TcAAP__fmB9Uw) people and sending 58 more to hospitals. More than 540 passengers were aboard the two trains, bound from Madrid to Seville. Spain's transport minister said the drivers were not at fault. A computer glitch had shut down the safety system on a 39-mile stretch, and a central control room then gave an ["inexplicable" order](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAUhJ8Gd6zg4NiXgiKNu5s2pcXP8fpELKwOxOS-feS8QprRFKNPM_Pzc__0lKk8f_gXun7UveBoGXtH3gPjQG6DyqicU0MmbCc9zx0ULFIrCXb3sdOFu56SOxABzYROr9bAYu1sptOFuOBsjtXPAYNdkor6Q5v1OMyiYQ52InfjtAKrlQGAB3zzCebVogKzqDWIWWGiXvnxq1LpJx75q17Ij1hfU3Zn7-8mzHcBm4BtjPHA31zvHXdAwHbjBWxa3f5DwEYF_7wzRR8yysoJWYYvGWvpXLOMWDqjpHJh6_T0HZP0R0eW7e2pyM63RvbtnNil96CcqS2rmNXz5Sn_q9X_78zLwd8AAAD__7H3isw) for the train to resume at full speed, possibly 124 mph, past an active stop signal. Spain's bullet-train network went 33 years without a fatal crash until this year. A January wreck involving the same two companies killed 46, and Spain's soccer federation [postponed 24](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAUhZ8GOwxeHB0Kim3sZtstDQPX8W4QDNwM8e037iv83UlOzsmX789rfTmKlD6_3YGWt7wmbDUiM5b1XbBhqY1SyyWGioWw7vTZV1AwyUFJMKvzTF9chy7YDRFQd2iH2WiYjBl1t9v5Oav3ALA9YAM1ojZm8067EY3SU3h2ZO-7QYEZlAaAHh4uwDgbVKAnNb_FqDAQ59L_zZR4xy1e-Yul9_noot2Zzyr0LwGLgKW11mM9010KWGr2HssdOJdLwLIKWCgIWB5Kq-k5DvcGQ8Ia3CV9Pp0MGGXBSx6O_Y5VnrnymRMGuTl2UXKOGLLk4ihJX1zdu2LD2ShGqtMsRvU5HMX_ePwzqV8L_wIAAP__6JmMRw) Copa del Rey games Wednesday night. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, facing an election in a month, declared three days of national mourning and called it "unacceptable for a country like Spain to [suffer two](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuxCAURE-DO1v449hQUKRxt2lTIgyf5UesWQFZlNtHzhXSjEYaaUbzPm_mZinRef-wD9QtZHNirwlbw2KOgh1L7XT2XJKvWAhrpHs0wGEdZz6CMtY1eqGZB68DIqAYUM-bErAqtYgh6mCtE-CBB9gkCpRy3Ra3yHBI8HL1A-mrbuagZi4AYII362HZFHIQK98OtnD01HKZvjKdLWJIP_mFZXL5MSQdW3tWJt4Z7Az23vvkjnrduHIG-2UZ7PVp6RxbudQVW-PYckKfx-_iLYN9KNo_O6VEdd3Ywu8PS-lvov0PzEvDbwAAAP__Ct54sw) high-speed rail accidents in the same year."
## 'Cruise for Life' Ends, Stranding 200 in Cambodia
A Florida-run cruise ship that sold cabins as permanent homes at sea abruptly [ended its three-year voyage](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdI7sMQFcuNgt6LLNFlsiGw8wKwdHHgPK3z_l_cKrr3R1zvn3mB6eEu3rH_9EV5c87XhxwlqxTKHghYUv2q9cUmQshLzRuk2goJNaSbCTnyudOOkmugUR0DTodG8NdNa2ptmcXrwNKiiIbRisWTpUqNseh37WqO_3htznTiuwWhkAuMHdR2h7iwpMp_ogWoWRai63_5n2uuGS3vnEcpvzs0luq_XFwvwSMAoYfZg_Cp9NwPj7YNqRWcB4UcG_NZe3gPFgOZeDGCVv9JK4R5ZrysEneea3X1F6Ji_jgVKbvoMB1NAUF18XpUTc9aJV69NT-kaoPwt3OvgKAAD__zEvguc) in Cambodia on Tuesday, giving its 203 passengers, mostly Americans, seven hours' notice to get off. Operator Villa Vie Residences blamed the Iran war, saying monthly fuel costs per cabin have jumped from about $1,800 to as much as [$8,000 in parts of Asia](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuhDAQBNCvMR3IXnwYFy7S0F3alMiHl2OjBZ9sB-v-PiK_kG6kkd5I83Wf756Yjuen39GVNc4H1sxYCqb5kbBiypWOGhOHjIkwb_TcZpAwtEq2YGe_FDpxVk1wKyJg36BTxvYwWKv7ZnOrt8ErD-NNwziagFrr9WYW1HowaGxD7uKUBKtkDwAd3HwAbSxK6AdpHkJLDFRi6r4jHWXDld_xxNQtcW_YbaW8sug_BEwCplprtxyP5SoFTBctYFLyyqOA6SRm356EbQzvnPHdrj_I7RJzyd1Wdm6SC69KzJQHI7R87p74b6r876DTwW8AAAD__0g_eR0). The company said it will try to restructure over the next 60 days, adding, _" No outcome is assured."_ Passengers said the trouble started earlier this year as fuel prices began to spike. Residents were asked for a [$3 million emergency loan](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCngW4jsxD4Xbi4hi7XXokWe4E9GRx5HVDe_pS8wtWfNJqZP4_pQRLlWH_Tzq4saTr40silcJ7mzBdnveS4Uo5BOQvrJus2ocEeGgNoJ_JFTp6aOriFGbmt2TWDbbG3tmvrzf009-DtTLYL89DdPzYvP37AJRARL7W4T1xj0DamRcQb3ilgN1g22PZmmKvOcJCS8u1vkqNsvMR3OjnffNrr6LZSnlq1vyocKxxXT89CcnywwvGUGAlOYUjhrcpvBT5CZFX4jgKfX6IMPu2sUBIQbBQLyAGe9jkFISCF5cURfNKioIlyhWOdXXheEqNoP1SdWXeS-G1U_u_H0-G_AAAA___d8osA) in April and $360,000 more for fuel recently, and a retired Wyoming couple said they were "tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money." The Odyssey left Belfast, Northern Ireland, in 2024 after months of delays, with suites ranging from $120,000 to $400,000. Some residents still hope to buy the ship themselves.

## E. coli Probe Eyes State Fair
Dallas County health officials are [lab-testing a cluster](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuunTAQhlcDnY9s8zAULtLQ3bQp0WAPMMqAj_BcIFl9xNlCur_49L9-fY1fQEz78hM29HLPadzxyowieIzbd6YALCSMdDNc-Ztk4ymNVttWGa1sP0IQOnGsoYx-0rE3JXrj-so645quXH1VhRimuo06GG2MqyttTQPYt2GanXMl-cfOaNsbo23VvLrGVc70Yeqx69zUFrXGSJKOl6woeEOe-U868XiFtJXsV5F3LqofhR0KO1zX9ZrTXT9DHqCwwyMLO0RghqxWBJZVpXmmQMBZ0X5iFlpAaF8UqpCYVICMWTHtvzGqLCCoZqBDffLVG-UD_02pPHx8X8RMuXVFrZcNiD_N5H8fPb39FwAA__-_3I9s) of E. coli cases among North Texas children to see whether the illnesses trace back to the petting zoo at the State Fair of Texas. Investigators are looking into [up to seven possible cases](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuupDAQRVdjMiPbfIwDB5OQ9aQTIn8KKMngFq6G7ln9E72Fl1bpXJ17_z2mh8OE-_LXbWDpPedph6skIIJj2l4Fg0uElADfyV3lhbQlnyclVM-l4MpMLhCeMLWuitaLaGQFVmrTKC11N1Sr7YbeNzLOfuj8IKUJupk72bY6RiVUayq0d5wUykgpVNPVQ6cbLU3wBoZB-561AiJSPmpageDtypw--YSjDnmrkl2JnoU1f5gamRqv66qDL3eP-8_U-EWYGu8TU2N0KbnCQ37t9OHAQ07Iw4opHrDzQo6Azw4P_uX4E4hwX_j_nDnuJxTCxRHmnedA2cPBb32mxuqw8XlhSlh6zVqxbA7TV5F-O-1p1U8AAAD___-jkTg), some of which have required intensive care. Doctors who alerted the county this week spotted a common thread among their patients: recent trips to the fair. The county hasn't confirmed the cases or a link to the fair and isn't calling it an outbreak. The fair said it [follows CDC-recommended precautions](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp_GdEb28GNcuNiG7m67JbLN5DLSECM8Cdl9-lXyCrf-9J0jnT9fy1ckpvv377hjkNetLHe8KqMInsv-qJQjCwkjvThe9UGycyoLGBi1NRr8ErPQE5c-NmtIZvW2wWCd78BZN0zNFtZuNCavpscJ0fcpRecS4JBil4bBQUPhjbMGvLUGuqGdBtc563PyOE0ujao3uJKUs5UNBV-x3vhveeLZ5rI3HDaRo6rul4JZwXxdV5u3s9zfq4L5c1Awx1MoMyqY18gcq64SBfUt0qlR58Kk_5WiAXo_dc62x3Y0Z1iPi5ipjk715nuPxB-p_DTWM8D_AAAA__9f-n-M) at animal exhibits and is cooperating fully with county health officials. Other fairs have faced the same problem. A 2025 outbreak linked to the Arizona State Fair's petting zoo hospitalized 13 children, and organizers [dropped the zoo entirely](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2unDAQxfGnMZ1X9pgvFy7S0N20KZHBA4wyYIRn2c19-mjzCqmP9NPR_9fX-BWJ6Vh_xh2DvJc8HvgqjCJ4jfuz0BxZSBjpzfFVniQ7T3kEA622RoMf4yx041jHKoXJJG8rDLbzDjrbNX21hQWtgan3Ljn0zs6tdQ0YaxdT-961UFH4cNaAt9aAax5907nO-nny2Pfd1KraYCLJ10M2FHzHsvCffOP1mPNecdhEzqLcDwWDgmHLOTEd-BkVDB9bwWCNgiFF5lg0HTcWoTUKFo16zkx65mcRvLQQJi1ZF4mCeol06RNF6Fj1d876N6Wit1xOksj0jUnBUF0hnS9iptJ2qjbrHon_XZP_TXoH-BsAAP__CAGM7A) for 2026, allowing guests to view farm animals only from a distance.
## Smuggling Boss 'Monstro' Gets Nine Years
A federal judge in El Paso sentenced a Mexican national known as "Monstro" to more than [nine years in federal prison](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu4yAURVeDOyLAdjAFxTTu_rRTWhgeCZoHRPDs-O9-lNnCr690dc7587V9uYSpPH67DJauWLcC745ABG3LR0_eISVCSBe6dz8SZdzrpoS6cym4MpvzlE7YJjcEu4tg5ABWajMqLfW8DE8bZyml0CGOZr_HGKKepXOLnowPk9qXIdnPnRTKSCnUON-WWY9aGr8bWBa939kkICSq7UZPILhcj_hdT2g3X_OA9kn06mz8xdTK1Po31ovOz8TU-rFhasXqHTK1AvKX65VHCNAccl-PRrxDISgeOn8e2RXe8_F4IDSea-nUKqfKDf8G1zpPhb9a6rUMzYbXOyGmftdsEo_sEv4Hop-GPK36FwAA___5UYwO) on Tuesday for a smuggling operation that ended with a migrant falling from a border fence. During a May 15, 2025, crossing near Tornillo, a migrant [fell from the fence](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2uqzAQhVcDnRG2CcaFi9fQ5bW3RAbGMJJ_InsIZPdXZAu3njlH33d-ntPTose4_bcBDF0uTRHO4oEI8hSOgov1hOQBL2_PciAFP6dJtKJnvGVCT3YhfMPU2Xo1c7tqXoPhSkuhuHoM9W6U6OXQDUovHZdOO9drOcu-7wah5apljeau463QnLdCPprhoaTiepk1DIOa-6prYUVKuaEdCC5bnP-kN-RmSaH2Zid6lUr-q8RYifE8z8alS9mjEMb7pRLjbVWJcT-CjayEY9tua5Yxbh7sCpmFFAvlxDagwjT7gM2FWUf3CbdsIzFnvS_M5RTYl4LNKd9RB3GBOpv1daL3WHpVde0WLPovIP112LcRvwEAAP___XaRbg) and broke a hip, the base of his spine, and a heel, injuries that required surgery. Border Patrol agents intercepted the group and arrested its guide. The [guide's phone held messages](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OnDAQAJ_GdD7Zexw-Chdp6L60KdGCF1hpwSd77-_tI_IKqUcajebPz_iDLHysv3GnqJ8ljwe9q5AqlXF_Vp5RlFWIP4Lv-mTdZcojOOisdxb6EWflF40tNilOLvW-oehDf4Xgw-3ebNEFgLadwS3T0kJKwaPvbhOmzoML0DccT5130Hvv4Hq73G_hGnw_Tz3d72HqTOsoseZy0Y2UPlgX-eYXlcuc90bipvqo5vrLwGBg2HJOwged0MBwug0M3hkYSOwDa7Z1f66rULF7PqqWbFfSanv7JSzV4qIn4rXgobZueM6oduOH5cMudMxkFxQxMDQlpsebRbh2wbRu3ZHlX5X-781XhL8BAAD__4XPiuI) with Manuel Alejandro Melendez-Cereceres, 42, who recruited drivers and coordinated stash houses and handoff points to move migrants deeper into the country. Agents arrested him at home in June 2025. He pleaded guilty June 11, 2026, and faces a $672,101 money judgment.
## Girl Cast as Seymour Sues District
A 17-year-old South Grand Prairie High School student [sued Grand Prairie ISD](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHO4yAQBOCnwR0R4MQOhYtr3P3XXmktsDgrrXEE-8f-3_6U6N7g6pFG882fr-ULiKmsv2HDSc68LwWPxiiCddm-G0VgIWGkk-Fo3yQbh31xxg3aGu38AlHohcsVujQFk7ztcLKj791ox9u9e0zYY0gJh2CzB589BuxzyGiizy7D0NH0rrPGeWuN62-X-23sR-tj8Hi_j2FQV4OJZK8XeaDgCS3zz_7Ceon71vH0EHk21f9SblZuPo7jUkJM-XjHys1vkXIz7xFYufkJFYs0nYlRf2yaTv1Pp4EZVyqrTtRipY0KCO1FQ9NPhh8doURkTBqyYNUrVdYMJTW9AaOuO6Ny89X44Wa8cnNXp_Q8iJnaMKqrWTcg_uyW__37Nbm_AQAA___Q6JoT) in federal court, arguing the district violated Title IX by removing her from the male lead in _Little Shop of Horrors_ because she is female. Ana Mota was cast as Seymour before administrators said a male student would replace her, [citing Senate Bill 12](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd0QwtsEULrZx97bd0hrwEI-EQwQ4zvv7VZ72D7a-0tE958_X-oWc-HH_jQfN7R3z-qCrJmqNynqclQOmxi0RvxNe9eR2JJ9XUGCkVhLciqHxi9YBu232anO6o1lb14PVdpy6ffbkezUF3Gg0Jug4qhgdRAuDMw4ddjx_cFqB01pBP96m0fZWu-AdTZP1RgyKNm653NpOjd5YY_rOLyq3kI8uzXtrzyr6XwIWAct1XbcrIn5GAQuWxiGRgOVjJmCh7QzYOD8ELD8wWb0G-U9P1ny2Xd4LPjb5LMiFSe5832UNe85JPhN-C1hgspKUHrzbghyUV3IIUclJayO11dbSYKLrTVfm7XlxSlyNFYO6H8jp53f7396vGf4GAAD__9relHs), the 2025 law restricting school instruction on gender identity. She declined a female part, and the district canceled the show. The district also said it pulled the musical to [comply with Senate Bill 12](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3unDAQxJ8GOiPbfBgKF2no_mlTorW9cCstGGEfcG8fccobpJtiNDO_-fMz_QAxbctvWNHme47ThldizBmPaX0n8sCZMiPdDFd6U17ZxUlL3QklhR4m8JlOnBoog3UyDKpEq8xQa6NM25cva-p-ruu-M6F1rnUaZxdMaH0XUA9GypLsE6ekHpSSum6rvjW1UYN3A_a9cV3RSAyU41HlF2a8Ic38iScelY9ryfaV856K-lehx0KP13VVc7ybB-QxFHp8ZKHH5YAtiP0AOggFpSBm8JjEPzIBzLjQtogvsaBbnBQZMsUtiadPeNg8MgaxM3zKw4b9ImZKnSkauaxA_J2U__fK0-q_AQAA__9ip41O), additionally pointing to the musical's themes of an abusive relationship. It declined to comment on the lawsuit, and students have moved on to producing the musical _Frozen_. The suit notes that the licensor permits cross-gender casting, and the bill doesn't ban it. It asks a judge to restore the musical with Mota as Seymour. Her attorney, David Coale, said the law has [some "pretty vague" provisions](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdI5sAzYuXFxDl2uvRMYs8UpLHOFN4N7-F3mFvxtppG_0zb_7dI9I-Hz8jRsEPtcyPeGoBMywT9u7YorEyAR4UjzqG3mjuUxGGSu1ksZPMTF-YOpis4RZLV43ELTzrXHa9UOTg4fVGu0Hq2aA2bdqtn1aujW1C1iX2gbDhdPKeK2Vafvb0LvWaZ9mD8PgZis6BQty2W-cgeGMdaX_5QP7LZWtoZCZX1W0f4QZhRk5Q0aiqxNmzGWDS0mYsXJkkEfklIUZrXbDoKz88mTGR5Y15VJIfn0lnpKQr1Rzecmyylz2vewXqdnD8jqQCKt1olOPLeJ3sOHfnvgJ5icAAP__F8iJAw).

subject: If you think Democrats have the November midterm elections in the bag, you’re wrong.
body:
At the DNC, we refuse to get complacent. In fact, we’re building the largest midterm operation in DNC history. [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/87341?t=1&akid=10149%2E22930333%2Ek3a3BQ)
---
Derek, if you think Democrats have the November midterm elections in the bag, you’re wrong. Let us explain: We have **_5 days left_** to help Democrats win up and down the ballot. A Blue Wave isn’t guaranteed — it’s something we have to fight for together, until the last race is called. **That’s why we’re reaching out to you.** If everyone who reads this email donated to the Democratic National Committee, we’d have the resources to continue supporting each of the 10,000 Democratic campaigns who are working to create a better future for all Americans. _But the unfortunate truth is that less than 10% of people will open this email, and less than 1% will chip in._ Derek, don’t wake up on November 4th wishing you had done more to [**help Democrats win.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-eom-october-2026.a6x_w1&refcode=em_20261029_10132_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10149%2E22930333%2Ek3a3BQ) At the DNC, we refuse to get complacent. # _**[SCOTUS Backs Trump On Deportations](https://links.thepricklypear.org/a/2777/click/202/71965/8ac96fa9684ac18f6c1877b9249fbb4bff30f458/7b35accfa8052dc77a3e83243b2e2da99257f9da)**_

---
On Oct. 27, the Supreme Court denied an emergency application from three cities and a legal-aid group that had asked it to suspend a Texas judge’s nationwide order barring immigration judges from “administratively closing,” or pausing, deportation cases. The one-line order, with no noted dissent, leaves that injunction in force.

---
On Oct. 26, a Ninth Circuit panel dismissed the Justice Department’s emergency appeal for lack of jurisdiction and denied its injunction request as moot, refusing to force California to segregate roughly 20,000 mail ballots the department had flagged as belonging to suspected noncitizens. A separate district-court hearing before Judge David O. Carter was set for Oct. 27.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Abdul El-Sayed’s final push
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Trump’s allies are pouring money into Michigan

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3069%2E4032634%2EVdzR3Z)
---
Abdul El-Sayed has built an extraordinary campaign by speaking directly to working people’s concerns with care, conviction, and joy. But Republicans and Trump-aligned super PACs are pouring tens of millions of dollars into ads for Mike Rogers. They’re relentless, and they have deep pockets. Now we’re down to the final five days. This is when the basics matter most: organizers knocking on doors, volunteers talking to neighbors, and voters getting the information they need before they cast their ballots. Every one of these actions before Election Day can make a difference. In 2024, Rogers narrowly lost his Michigan Senate race by fewer than 19,000 votes. In a state with millions of voters, it shows us just how much a few votes in each precinct can tip the scales. If we want a Democratic Senate that can hold Trump accountable and fight to bring down costs, we cannot afford to lose this seat. We need the resources to compete right through Election Day. [**Will you split a $28 contribution between Abdul’s campaign and this grassroots movement to help reach voters during this final push?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3917?amount=28&t=8&akid=3069%2E4032634%2EVdzR3Z)

up.

The only thing preventing us from doing that is a lack of resources.

If we see a surge in grassroots support today, we can send a few more

in a few more ZIP codes, and truly seize the moment in these last few
days.

That difference matters. **And with Election Day just five days away, we need to make sure voters hear it.**

This past week Microsoft offered [buyouts](https://substack.com/redirect/68f7569a-e462-4a4e-b6bf-b443bc177b8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to 60,000 employees, representing about 27% of their global workforce. They are transitioning some of their operations to AI.
That is staggering. Each of those employees will have to bite hard and make a tough call. If you don't take the buyout, you might get a pink slip next year on much worse terms. If you do take the offer, you will get a runway of several months . . . and then what? I'd expect a lot of people to take the buyout while the getting is good. Your employer just told you that your services are no longer needed or valued. If you stick around at that point, you're really asking for the door.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aa287b86-4eac-4ff5-bd40-cc0e5cae330b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I've walked the Microsoft corporate campus at Redmond - it's essentially the equivalent of a small city. There were definitely too many people walking around, if you know what I mean. "What do all of these people do?" occurred to me. Still, having 1 out of 4 of them getting Thanos-snapped off the campus is wild stuff.
There are almost too many announcements to keep straight. In the last week alone:
American Express said it was [laying off](https://substack.com/redirect/8b6961a4-bb7d-4dc3-9e08-3df397e25e04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 3850 workers even as their profits went up.
The Dutch government said it would [replace 25,000 workers](https://substack.com/redirect/7d6f1a6d-327e-45bc-812e-dcb912716391?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with AI. This is about 16% of their civil workforce. For a government to make a move like this is huge. The equivalent move in the U.S. would affect about 400,000 workers.
Getty Images, the behemoth repository of photographic images, [declared bankruptcy](https://substack.com/redirect/81785f0f-65f6-4e8f-88bb-515f2a2c980a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Apparently no one wants to pay for fancy photographs when AI can just conjure them up for you for pennies. Say goodbye to photography as a field that would enable anyone to make a decent living.
Goldman Sachs published a [new study](https://substack.com/redirect/87dc3f1a-9afa-473a-832f-c298abe60bc1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) saying that industries that adopt AI see lower job growth. I wonder why.
And of course Anthropic filed its S-1 in preparation for one of the [biggest IPOs of all time](https://substack.com/redirect/a5ca3441-d06d-412b-9233-d15d6286a311?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Analysts pored over it. It's looking like a $1.5 trillion target valuation for Anthropic's debut. Revenue was up to $16.3 billion for the first six months of this year, up 14x. There were some trouble spots in the document: there are a lot of long-term commitments for compute costs, a slightly less stupendous growth rate moving forward, and the risk factors have to be seen to be believed. Things like "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" actually make it in. The IPO is expected in mid-November.
Any of these stories should be enormous, as should the [hack of Quest Diagnostics](https://substack.com/redirect/5f5d981c-a938-46ab-a35b-69188fcf9a0d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week and the advent of "Black October" for cybersecurity experts. But there are almost too many things going on to keep track of.
Here's a summary: Humans are being kicked to the curb in unprecedented ways. The reaction to this will play out at the ballot box next Tuesday. But the troubles - and the work to rebuild - are just beginning. Change your password.
I spent the weekend in South Dakota where I campaigned with [Brian Bengs](https://substack.com/redirect/87d6ec0c-34ad-4737-8381-2e367bab0f1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who is running for U.S. Senate and is tied with the incumbent Mike Rounds. Please consider donating to [Brian Bengs](https://substack.com/redirect/87d6ec0c-34ad-4737-8381-2e367bab0f1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Todd Achilles](https://substack.com/redirect/f98f84f3-fa6f-4477-a974-470d14ef9d92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and/or [Seth Bodnar](https://substack.com/redirect/5fefb9c4-d204-441d-90c0-30c253d1fc63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or to [Forward](https://substack.com/redirect/01e3d004-7492-4e49-9898-26653aa83d4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) which is elevating some of the most game-changing candidates in the country. I’m so proud of my team...!

I'm so proud of my team...!
| Our team hit a major milestone recently, Peter...
Our volunteers have officially knocked on 100,000 doors this election cycle!
---
I'm so proud and grateful for our hard-working volunteers, and I'm so grateful to have you in my corner. Your donations played a large role in making this happen. clean_body: I just left South Carolina. This race is neck and neck, and Darline needs us now. | Fellow Patriot, On Monday, I was in South Carolina, on the campaign trail with Darline Graham. I want to tell you what I saw, because this race is closer than anyone in Washington wants to admit. It is neck and neck. Election Day is less than a week away, and Darline's seat could swing either way. Here's what I told the folks there: -> You don't want a Senate run by Chuck Schumer. -> You don't want Elizabeth Warren to chair the Senate Banking Committee. -> And you don't want Bernie Sanders setting environmental policy that kills jobs in South Carolina. That's the radical Democrat agenda, and it's what Annie Andrews would be voting for. She's raised over $25 million - nearly $4 million in the last couple of weeks - from liberal donors who don't share South Carolina's values. She built her campaign attacking Lindsey, and now her whole mission is to defeat his sister. Darline stands for common sense: low taxes, good jobs, and backing the police. She won't vote to put violent criminals back on the street or to let boys compete in girls' sports. She has thirty years of experience working for the people of her state, and she has a backbone. What Darline doesn't have is Hollywood money. Schumer needs JUST FOUR SEATS to take the majority, and he's betting South Carolina hands him one because Darline is being outspent after running two elections back-to-back. Fellow Patriot, races this close are decided in the final days by who can stay on the air, keep volunteers knocking doors, and get voters to the polls. They tried this playbook on me in Texas. National Democrats dumped millions to attack me because they thought the bigger bank account would win. Now I'm making a personal plea: show up for Darline. | | | | | | We have less than a week. Let's not sit this one out. I'll keep this brief:

We’re in the final week before Election Day.

I’m working with my fellow Democrats to support strong candidates across
the country and build the momentum we need to take back the Senate.

But before Election Day arrives, I also want to hear directly from you.

name: Kristan Hawkins
subject: they're getting doors slammed in their faces
body:
Two weeks until Election Day. Our student canvassers need to know you have their backs.

*|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | |
---
| | [](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0DGu3CAQxvHT4G4tGHhgCopIK3cvbUprDLMsijEI2I1y-8hKcoFX_0ejn74fn9snpiOd8TtmcrHUurW-jSf9bhRpjHTGUErr_cCcKWzAQd8Ev4Hd0I_0pk3hFJxCrbTWEzlhrARjtITp6ZT1fDHBWqnNLjWCJw_igxaJBnYQU3LXQ8HBClBc8vkhjfhY1B6Mt4u1O1OcQhqlzZetUU-BzpHwmH3J0-GeY9TO5DcGK4O1k381mvt4XVf9UdqRHnRByzmXFhmsFW8eG1X0PzESaCbX3jyTd8q1MdC5xxSYvF8qYSsy0K-RN4-5YornVf6J_5dyDjoHk_dLODUX6q90HKlrwxSPGdNf6_jqum8HfwIAAP__yOiKfw)

Dear Pro-Life Friend,

Our volunteer student canvassers have been through the wringer these past couple of months.

Doors get slammed in their faces. They get shouted off stoops. And sometimes, even worse things happen.

So, I’ve told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two weeks.

Pro-Life Friend, our student canvassers know what’s on the line.

They know if abortion-loving leftists seize power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies.

And they know the job’s not done yet.

But right now, they could use a little moral boost heading into the final weeks before Election Day on Tuesday, November 3rd.

[That’s why I’m hoping you’ll prayerfully consider sending a Care Package to one of our door-to-door canvassers](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0DGu3CAQxvHT4G4tGHhgCopIK3cvbUprDLMsijEI2I1y-8hKcoFX_0ejn74fn9snpiOd8TtmcrHUurW-jSf9bhRpjHTGUErr_cCcKWzAQd8Ev4Hd0I_0pk3hFJxCrbTWEzlhrARjtITp6ZT1fDHBWqnNLjWCJw_igxaJBnYQU3LXQ8HBClBc8vkhjfhY1B6Mt4u1O1OcQhqlzZetUU-BzpHwmH3J0-GeY9TO5DcGK4O1k381mvt4XVf9UdqRHnRByzmXFhmsFW8eG1X0PzESaCbX3jyTd8q1MdC5xxSYvF8qYSsy0K-RN4-5YornVf6J_5dyDjoHk_dLODUX6q90HKlrwxSPGdNf6_jqum8HfwIAAP__yOiKfw)**.**

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

These young women and men will be on their feet for hours, walking door to door. And knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going.

Of course, I could tell our door knockers to go home.

I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead.

But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad ever could. And the effect doesn’t disappear after one election.

**Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote again in the next election, too.**

And, it costs us less than $3 for every door we knock.

This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that’s needed to turn out every pro-life voter.

Last cycle, this approach worked.
**> >> In Oklahoma,** our canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion state senators who killed our legislation to stop chemical abortion pill trafficking. Voters threw them out.

**> >> In South Carolina,** we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who killed our “Life at Conception Act.” They lost too.

**> >> In North Carolina,** 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries.
The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to give up and go home during this final stretch.

It’s true they have the money, the media, and the institutions.

But what they don’t have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger’s door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words, and still go knock on the next door.

That grit and determination is what wins elections.

Most of you know me as President Bartlet from The West Wing. But many years before my term as TV president, I was in a film called Apocalypse Now.
For those of you who haven’t seen it, Apocalypse Now follows an American soldier on a journey up the rivers of Vietnam. It’s a story all about the horrors of a war that still affects us to this day.
_The Turek family knows that firsthand._
Josh Turek’s father, John, joined the Navy on his 18th birthday. He served in Vietnam for 22 months, but the effects of war lingered with him long after he returned home.
His son, Josh, was born with spina bifida caused by Agent Orange exposure. Josh underwent 21 painful surgeries as a young boy, dealt with terrible bullying, and struggled to navigate life in a wheelchair.
Through sheer will, he became a celebrated athlete in wheelchair basketball, winning a scholarship, playing professionally, and even taking home two gold medals for Team USA at the Paralympics.
Next, Josh decided to give politics a shot. He served two successful terms in the Iowa State House before launching his United States Senate campaign last year.
Now, Josh is the Democratic nominee for the Senate seat currently held by Joni Ernst, and is tied with his Republican opponent in the polls.
**That’s one heck of a story, don’t you agree?**
Josh Turek has the resilience and strength to win Iowa. **These qualities make him Democrats’ secret weapon in the fight for control of the Senate.**

clean_body: | | | ** It’s Martin Sheen. After more than half a century as an actor, I know a thing or two about a good story. Josh Turek, Iowa’s next U.S. Senator, has a story like no other. I’ll get to that shortly. But first I have a message, not as an actor, but as a fellow patriot. Iowa’s open Senate seat is Democrats’ ticket to retaking the Senate and protecting our Constitution for generations to come. This is not a race any of us can watch from the sidelines. Josh has the strength, the skill, and support to win, but he doesn’t accept money from corporate pacs. His campaign is powered by donations from Americans like you and me. | Most of you know me as President Bartlet from The West Wing. But many years before my term as TV president, I was in a film called Apocalypse Now. For those of you who haven’t seen it, Apocalypse Now follows an American soldier on a journey up the rivers of Vietnam. It’s a story all about the horrors of a war that still affects us to this day. The Turek family knows that firsthand. Josh Turek’s father, John, joined the Navy on his 18th birthday. He served in Vietnam for 22 months, but the effects of war lingered with him long after he returned home. His son, Josh, was born with spina bifida caused by Agent Orange exposure. Josh underwent 21 painful surgeries as a young boy, dealt with terrible bullying, and struggled to navigate life in a wheelchair. Through sheer will, he became a celebrated athlete in wheelchair basketball, winning a scholarship, playing professionally, and even taking home two gold medals for Team USA at the Paralympics. Next, Josh decided to give politics a shot. He served two successful terms in the Iowa State House before launching his United States Senate campaign last year. Now, Josh is the Democratic nominee for the Senate seat currently held by Joni Ernst, and is tied with his Republican opponent in the polls. That’s one heck of a story, don’t you agree? Josh Turek has the resilience and strength to win Iowa. These qualities make him Democrats’ secret weapon in the fight for control of the Senate. Josh will make a first-rate senator. He can count on my full support, and I hope he can count on yours as well. So I ask you today to please join me in electing a great future senator this November. ** Sincerely, Martin Sheen Actor, Activist, and Proud Supporter of Josh Turek is a Federal PAC created to support six carefully selected rural and progressive Democrats. name: Bill Nye
subject: What happens in Michigan also happens to America
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3792%2E251025%2E5bnS2f ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3792%2E251025%2E5bnS2f ]Abdul for US Senate

[ Bill ]Bill Nye

Hi Peter,
it’s Bill Nye.

I’ll get right to it: [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1756?t=1004&akid=3792%2E251025%2E5bnS2f ]I’m reaching out to ask for your help electing
Dr. Abdul El-Sayed to the U.S. Senate from Michigan by volunteering.

I’d like you to consider the following:

Pollution is chemistry. When a refinery releases sulfur dioxide, the gas
drifts into nearby neighborhoods and ends up in the lungs of the people
who live closest to it.

That part is just basic science, and we can’t change the laws of nature.
Whether the company gets permission to release more of those toxins,
unrestricted, is where politics comes into play.

Abdul understands that connection through his studies in medical school.
He sees how something like scrapping limits on toxic “forever chemicals”
in our drinking water can lead to those chemicals end up being consumed by
Michigan families.

A lot of folks in Washington seem to have forgotten that science is
written into the Constitution. Article I, Section 8, Clause 8 gives
Congress the job “to promote the Progress of Science.” Standing up for
science isn’t partisan. It’s about as American as it gets.

That’s why I’m with Abdul.

Abdul trained as a doctor and an epidemiologist. He follows the evidence.
He takes on corporate polluters. And he sticks to his values by not taking
a dime from corporate PACs. No polluter can buy Abdul.

Abdul is looking out for the future.

But that future won’t build itself. It starts with electing people who
believe in it, including Abdul.

Election Day is in 6 days. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1756?t=1005&akid=3792%2E251025%2E5bnS2f ]Will you sign up to volunteer so that
Michigan sends someone to the Senate who respects science and can’t be
bought?

If you can't canvass in person, [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1619?t=1006&akid=3792%2E251025%2E5bnS2f ]phone banking is also a very impactful
option that you can do everyday and from anywhere.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1756?t=1007&akid=3792%2E251025%2E5bnS2f ]Volunteer ››

Onward,
Bill Nye

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Emails like this help us stay connected with grassroots supporters like you, so thank you for taking the time to read this message. To contribute via check, please address it to Abdul for U.S. Senate, PO Box 126, St. Clair Shores, MI 48080.

Receive Fewer Emails: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/?t=1008&akid=3792%2E251025%2E5bnS2f
Update Your Information: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/signup/update-your-information
Unsubscribe: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=1009&akid=3792%2E251025%2E5bnS2f

Email us: info@abdulformichigan.com
Volunteer: https://go.abdulforsenate.com/

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

Peter, it’s Cait Conley. Votes are already being cast in NY-17 and our campaign is in a strong position to beat Mike Lawler. That would not be possible without the help and support of tens of thousands of people like you who have chipped in a little bit here and there over the last 18 months. **But I do have some bad news to share:**
* Mike Lawler has been outraising us during this final stretch.
* We have not raised nearly the amount of money we need to meet our final budget

This is on track to be the most competitive and expensive House race in the country. Mike Lawler won his first election by just 1820 votes. If we’re going to win here, I need your help. [Please, chip in $10 to my campaign today.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcynj_UHKTnEbFJuXRbcU0RusMeK8Uw0hMFlhZHdKfCOjybhkwBJDK2RJ3Dwe-jKXM4AmaBsUfzBLb9AAHsHmniT24pSRa3DIiMkGuDI7hJSfM7AiZ5dhrVYRtQuolQ4BSmDgWJ-PrUjTG77dGY3ujp5lb3IJVaFNkGV3GiTjSLRIopHeAf_BrJ0Z4ankKIA8WZDfuCicxE6woQVH5sOikRaPxRbMHCbHt_nxg4HWThKmHGLFq0q2NqE3sCBH3AUIz_/4va/vl2SjgmeR4W2alQr2tJ86A/h1/h001.sS2m-6RSyyBBLEL86P9wVAAhom4SiGEcDdCImHUoxZk) | [DONATE »](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcynj_UHKTnEbFJuXRbcU0RusMeK8Uw0hMFlhZHdKfCOjybhkwBJDK2RJ3Dwe-jKXM4du6lLsakqIhBkrK8revpquAnn_AZc4bsHdOpjFw2rneBf296-tVbd0g4QYY3uyFanOh04wE7IcE9o_6xWxZHaxkdtwM4yrxDgDwKLBWv7fZ4BgEBCM5KJpf5K_5le3apO69hbfRN94h08qkKdeA1PnfDI1p1n2-Bg4Yt70MztgJzgrTp6-S-S7WCFuaEDaL_/4va/vl2SjgmeR4W2alQr2tJ86A/h2/h001.Oplph9cHPU7VX-HoW6QlSOE2ZetC2t_-dbsweWWP7L4)

In 2024, this was one of just three districts nationwide that voted for Kamala Harris and a Republican. Mike Lawler survived because billionaires and MAGA super PACs spent an absurd sum of money in the final sprint to November.
They’re running the exact same play this year. But we do not have to let our district be defined by men like Mike Lawler.
I’m running for Congress because the people running this administration do not share our values—or the values of the generations of Americans who fought and sacrificed to make this country better.
This chapter in American history is not yet written. Who we become, the values that define us, that is up to what we do over the next week.
[So I’m respectfully asking you to chip in $10, or whatever you can afford, to help us close the gap with Lawler. Early voting has started—your support makes a major difference in our ability to close out this race and reach every possible voter.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcynj_UHKTnEbFJuXRbcU0RusMeK8Uw0hMFlhZHdKfCOjybhkwBJDK2RJ3Dwe-jKXM49biICrxg8GyyeSbbdspqcAxIKbrHgK7wxh_drF8C9NJX1WVa6dVe-ru6ty6oj9mV3Hrs8yTw5S787Ih5rEX-zvr9TLsOFi8s96pi-Pz3TeT5FNfyLlkxZEySHxalEpbFgBdvPaq-WgHoJRHry_uJzhYRvvwq84O_LsdE8L42X9S-mmYeCXjF7_bRL5W8R0GD/4va/vl2SjgmeR4W2alQr2tJ86A/h3/h001.GAgR9vKLKLCKn9ILZko8dXwfttYa59iqnRuGF7-QXRg)

Cait Conley

| | Peter, The election is already happening. Early ballots are flooding in across Minnesota, where **Peggy Flanagan's** dead-heat race for the first Native American woman EVER in the Senate is being decided vote by vote, today. Alaskans are already deciding whether **Mary****Peltol** a flips the majority-maker seat — while the DOJ lawsuit meant to rattle their heads toward dismissal. body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, Team Shapiro
here. This campaign is built on grassroots power, and we try never to lose
sight of who makes up that foundation: You.

So we’re not going to treat you like an ATM.

We’re not going to invent a deadline that doesn’t exist. We’re not going
to tell you your donation triples when it doesn’t. And we’re not going to
write to you tomorrow pretending tonight was your last chance when it
wasn’t.

Here’s what’s real,
Derek: On Saturday at midnight,
we’ll face our last End-of-Month deadline before Election Day. It’s not a
gimmick. It’s the last major deadline before Pennsylvania’s future — our
country’s future — changes forever.

But here’s what's also real:

In 2016, Donald Trump won Pennsylvania by 1%. In 2020, Joe Biden won
Pennsylvania by 1%. In 2024, Republicans won a Senate seat by 0.22%. Time
and again, Pennsylvania elections have come down to the smallest
make-or-break margins — and those margins can shape the direction of the
entire country.

That’s why we can’t treat this race like anything is guaranteed.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/21886?t=1001&akid=837%2E245147%2EzOVLYI ]So please,
Derek: With only five days left
until Pennsylvanians finish voting and our last End-of-Month deadline fast
approaching, will you rush $25 to help us fund the
final weekend of canvassing, keep our ads on the air until the moment
polls close, and put real people at polling places on Tuesday morning?

After the EPA handed Louisiana Class VI primacy in early 2024 (the power to permit CO2 injection wells itself), the state became the carbon-capture capital of America. The Environmental Integrity Project counts at least 65 proposed projects -- more than any other state -- with roughly 50 well applications from 33 projects in review. Louisiana Economic Development touts $23 billion in announced CCS investment; an LSU Energy Institute analysis identified 13 projects worth ~$48 billion. Marquee examples: CF Industries' ~$4 billion Donaldsonville ammonia complex with ExxonMobil (the largest CCS project in the U.S.), and Air Products' $4.5 billion blue-hydrogen plant in Ascension Parish.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c9496106-103c-4086-a6cc-faae8db61614?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The sticker prices are private capital, but the engine is public money: the federal 45Q tax credit pays $85 per ton sequestered, plus state incentives, lease revenues, and DOE grants. That's the familiar pattern taxpayers have financed for decades, and the watchdog TCSW summary is blunt: after billions in subsidies, most past CCS projects were abandoned or underperformed, leaving taxpayers holding the bag. ...

I've got a message for the billion-dollar corporations looking to build massive data centers in our communities: **Our neighborhoods are not for sale. Not our land. Not our water. Not our electricity grid. And certainly not our families' futures.** Texas families are already getting squeezed by rising electricity bills, housing costs, and the price of just about everything else. My answer is that it will not change if we wait for Washington to reform itself. It changes when we send people who commit to reform before they arrive. That is why I joined Take BAC Congress. Here are the five points.
1. **Term limits for Congress.** Twelve years, then make room for someone new.
2. **No stock trading while serving.** Members of Congress should not profit from insider trading.
3. **A five-year lobbying ban.** No walking from the Capitol straight into a lobbying firm.
4. **Overturn Citizens United.** Voters, not unlimited corporate money, should decide our elections.
5. **An enforceable ethics code for the Supreme Court.** Every public servant should answer to the public.

subject: We can END Trump’s presidency in five days
body:
When Donald Trump tried to rig the election before a single vote was cast
by redistricting in Texas, we fought fire with fire in California and we
won.

Now we have to finish the job.

We gave Democrats a chance to flip five House seats, but there are two of
those races that are still in doubt.

And they need your help, desperately. Even at this late hour. It could be
the difference.

So consider this my last-ditch request for Richard Pan and Randy Villegas.
If you're looking for a good place to make one last donation before the
election, this is it.

Contribute to them using the link below, they will see your donation come
through immediately, and they can put it right to work in the way they
believe gives them the best chance to win.

Folks, we can effectively end Donald Trump's presidency in just a few
days. We can put a check on his power if we can take back the House.

But heaven help us if we come up short. There is absolutely no telling
what Trump is capable of in his final two years with unchecked power.

This is it -- all hands on deck moment for Democrats. And these are two of
the House races that will make all the difference.

and Randy Villegas. The amount doesn't matter as much as the donation

they can.

| | | | Peter, Five days left. If your ballot is still on the kitchen table, I want you to see who's standing with me before you fill it out. **Labor unions across the district.** The Washington State Labor Council, AFL-CIO, the Washington State Building & Construction Trades Council, the Spokane Regional Labor Council, IAM District 751, the Washington Machinists Council, IBEW Local 73, LiUNA Local 238 and UA Local 44. **National organizations defending our nation, our rights, our earned benefits.** National Security Leaders for America, Foreign Policy for America, and The Steady State. EMILYs List. The Center for Free Thought Equality. The Alliance for Gun Responsibility Victory Fund and Gun Sense Voter. The Alliance of Retired Americans and the Retired Public Employees Council of Washington. The National Women's Political Caucus. Elect Democratic Women. **Democrats from the Asotin, Columbia, Ferry, Franklin, Pend Oreille, Spokane, Stevens, Walla Walla, and Whitman county parties;** the 4th, 6th, 7th, and 9th LD Democrats, Washington State Stonewall Democrats, and EWU Student Democrats. **And neighbors from every corner of the district,** including State Senator Marcus Riccelli, State Representatives Timm Ormsby and Natasha Hill, Spokane County Commissioner Chris Jordan, Spokane City Council President Betsy Wilkerson – and Rich Kuhling, former chair of the Spokane County Republican Party. Help us get this list out to voters who haven’t made up their mind yet by [**_contributing an extra $5 or $10 to our Voter Outreach Fund (Week 0)_**](https://us.list-manage.com/kzrFXfASSGh?e=a7b299e420&c2id=1b040b68f1d062d0c966c24dae99fcb4). Then please forward this to a friend who hasn't voted yet. This race will come down to just a few votes. Thank you,
Carmela

Twice in four years, a six-justice conservative majority has accomplished what no Democratic committee, consultant, or candidate could: turning a courthouse ruling into a turnout event. On June 24, 2022, in 'Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization', the Court repealed a federal abortion right and watched college-educated women answer. On April 29, 2026, in 'Louisiana v. Callais', it struck down Louisiana's second majority-black congressional district and hollowed out Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act -- and watched black voters answer. Different constituencies, different grievances, same mechanism. Tell people the law now considers them expendable, and they will show you what expendable looks like in November.
**The Dobbs ledger**
The 2022 evidence is the cleanest demonstration that grievance out-organizes ground game. KFF's AP VoteCast analysis found that in the states voting directly on abortion that year, roughly four in ten voters said the overturning of 'Roe' was a major reason they turned out; among women under fifty, between 45 and 55 percent said so. NBC's exit polls found abortion was the number-one issue for women voters, white college-educated voters, early voters, and Latino voters -- and those who ranked it first broke for Democrats 76 to 23. White college women, about 17 percent of the electorate, voted Democratic 56 to 42.
The registration data ran ahead of the votes. Catalist's post-election study found a disproportionate share of women registering in contested states after the ruling; Kansas had given the preview in August, when its referendum drew near-record primary turnout and women became the clear majority of new registrants in the weeks that followed. On Election Day, six states voted on abortion measures -- more than in any prior year -- and every one broke in the pro-choice direction. About six in ten voters told pollsters they were dissatisfied with 'Dobbs', including 27 percent of Republicans. A projected red wave arrived a ripple: the slimmest out-party House gain in decades, and a Senate that stayed Democratic.
The honest caveat: Brookings' turnout analysis found national turnout by sex barely different from 2018 -- the surge was surgical, concentrated in contested states and among college graduates, not universal. But midterms are won surgically. Michigan was the exhibit: turnout jumps among white college graduates, women, and young voters, a re-elected Democratic governor, and an abortion-rights amendment carried by double digits.
**The Callais ledger**
The 2026 evidence is younger -- Election Day is still a week out -- but it is already legible in the early vote. 'Callais', decided 6-3 with Justice Alito writing, held that Louisiana's 2024 map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander because race predominated in drawing a second majority-black district, and that Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act requires no such district at all. The Legal Defense Fund called it an evisceration of Section 2; within two weeks, Louisiana, Alabama, Tennessee, and South Carolina were moving to eliminate majority-black districts of their own, and roughly 140 majority-minority House districts suddenly sat inside the blast radius. For black voters, it read as act three: 'Shelby County' gutted preclearance in 2013; 'Callais' gutted Section 2 in 2026 -- the Act's two engines disassembled thirteen years apart by successive majorities.
The answer came at the polls. The Legal Defense Fund reported that in Louisiana's May election, black voters made up nearly 36 percent of the electorate, though they are 32 percent of the state. VoteHub's analysis found black turnout surging across Southern primaries more than two months after the ruling, even as Republican legislatures accelerated redrawing Democratic seats. And Bloomberg's data, published October 27, found Southern black voters casting early ballots at a record pace a week before Election Day -- in Georgia and North Carolina outpacing both the 2018 and 2022 midterms and outpacing white and Hispanic voters. Advocates attribute it directly to the gerrymandering backlash. Early votes are not election results; the verdict arrives November 3. But the motivation is no longer hypothetical.
**What the symmetry says**
On the merits, the two cases share almost nothing -- one about a liberty, one about a map, decided by the same six votes. As turnout strategy, they are _identical_. Each ruling told a Democratic-leaning bloc that a protection it had organized its civic life around could be deleted, six to three, in a morning. Each bloc answered with the only power the ruling left it: the franchise. The Court registered no one, knocked no doors, sent no texts. It simply ruled, and the queues did the rest.
Republicans won both cases outright -- and in both years lost the argument the cases created. 'Dobbs' handed the GOP the policy it had pursued for fifty years and accelerated the loss of the college-educated women it was already shedding by inches. 'Callais' handed the party its maps and manufactured the turnout surge now making those maps expensive to hold. That is the paradox of governing by gavel: you can win the holding and lose the holdouts, the voters who decline to be dissuaded.
The Supreme Court helped Democrats get to the polls twice because it is the only institution with the authority to make those two blocs feel the law itself move against them. Legislation feels negotiable; a holding does not. Judges think in doctrines. Voters think in headlines, and the headlines wrote themselves: your pregnancy can be criminalized; your district can be dissolved because it was drawn for you.
Who decided? In both cases, six votes did. And in both cases, the lines outside the polling places decided what those votes were worth.
