Photo by Guerinault Louis/Anadolu via Getty Images. Thursday, October 29, 2026 -** Iran: Vice President JD Vance requests renewed talks in letter to Iran's security chief. Associated Press: U.S. warns regional allies to prepare for possible renewed war in Iran. Iran claims three oil tankers struck mines near Strait of Hormuz. Iran claims capture of one U.S. spy drone, downing of another over Hormuz. War Secretary Pete Hegseth fires Pentagon's top military planner. Palestine: Israeli drone strike in central Gaza kills two Palestinians. Israeli forces demolish homes in the occupied West Bank as Hebron siege enters seventh day. Israeli settlers beat U.S. journalist and Russian activists in West Bank. Gaza Health Ministry stresses urgency of increased medical evacuations through Rafah. Yemen: Nearly 1,700 killed and 281,000 displaced in Yemen since August. Ansarallah reports 101 airstrikes by Saudi-backed forces across Yemen. Human Rights Watch: Ansarallah depriving civilians of food, medicine in Taiz. Lebanon: Hezbollah leader calls Israeli election results "an expression of defeat," rejects disarmament. U.S.: DoorDash buys Instacart for $17 billion. Dolores Huerta, labor leader and civil rights figure who co-founded United Farm Workers, dies at 96. Fed holds rates steady. Leak exposes records of more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors, including undercover ICE agents. Judge rejects Trump administration bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots. DOJ turned a rights-group informant into the government's own. Trump administration issues more than 100 subpoenas for voter records in at least 13 states ahead of midterms. California elites spend $612 million to defeat billionaire tax. CNN Senate poll finds Democrats up in Michigan, Kansas, Maine, and Texas. International: Russian drone strike on Ukraine train station kills at least 14. Flavio Bolsonaro declares himself Brazil's rightful "leader" after arriving in Miami. Pakistani court sentences human rights lawyers to 10 years in prison. Clashes on Pakistan-Afghan border kill one. South Korean prosecutors again seek death penalty for ex-President Yoon Suk-yeol. Iraq Prime Minister visits Damascus. North Korea fires short-range ballistic missiles into Sea of Japan. El Salvador to send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti, increasing military presence. U.S. sanctions Rwanda defense ministry and Rwandan financial institution over the eastern Congo conflict. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Vance requests renewed talks in letter to Iran 's security chief: Vice President JD Vance a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing renewed direct negotiations as the Trump administration considers launching a short, intense military campaign against Iran after next week's U.S. midterm elections, the Wall Street Journal reported. The letter was delivered through Qatari mediators on Sunday. In it, Vance proposed a meeting as early as next week, to be potentially held in Qatar or Turkey. Vance would lead the U.S. delegation, the New York Times . Discussions have so far focused on a negotiating framework rather than specific terms, as Washington demands upfront nuclear concessions while Tehran seeks immediate economic relief. President Donald Trump confirmed on Wednesday that he had approved Vance's outreach, but he characterized it as an effort to facilitate medical supplies. "They need help with medical supplies and various things," Trump told reporters. "He asked me what I thought. I said, 'If you want to do that, that's OK.'" Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on X: "While our Brave Armed Forces are fully prepared to defend the Homeland, Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed." He added that Tehran remained "in close and ongoing contact with intermediaries" to explore implementing Iran's seven-day plan "in even less than a week." AP: U.S. warns regional allies to prepare for possible renewed war in Iran: U.S. officials told several Middle East allies to prepare for renewed military action against Iran after the U.S. midterm elections next week, two diplomats briefed on the matter . The diplomatic sources told the AP that the U.S. informed regional allies that the new round of military action could last for several days, but regional officials are preparing for Iranian retaliation that could lead to a longer fight. U.S. officials urged regional allies to take precautionary measures against Iranian retaliatory strikes targeting energy facilities and other crucial infrastructure, according to AP. President Trump has not made a final decision on whether to carry out new strikes against Iran, the diplomats said. Iran claims three oil tankers struck mines near Strait of Hormuz: Three oil tankers after striking naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and Thursday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday. The IRGC said the vessels had switched off their radar and navigation systems, ignored warnings, and attempted to pass through an "unauthorized" southern route. Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations said on Thursday that a ship had been spotted on fire nine nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. The crew's condition, the extent of the damage, and the environmental impact remain unknown. IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebi reiterated that the Strait of Hormuz remains "under the strategic control of the Iranian armed forces and will never be opened until the Islamic Republic's conditions are fully met," in comments quoted by the Fars news agency on Thursday. Iran claims capture of one U.S. spy drone, downing of another over Hormuz: The IRGC on Thursday that it captured an intact U.S. MQM-170 reconnaissance and decoy drone west of the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC electronic warfare unit allegedly took control of the aircraft's guidance systems and took it down. The IRGC said, without providing evidence, that the U.S. deployed the drone to identify Iranian air defense positions along the Persian Gulf coast and had taken off from an unnamed Gulf country. Separately, the IRGC said that it intercepted and destroyed a U.S. MQ-1 drone over the eastern Strait of Hormuz, the 14th MQ-1 drone it says it has shot down. The U.S. military has not commented on the IRGC's claims. Hegseth fires Pentagon 's top military planner: U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth Brett Sylvia, the Pentagon's top military planner. Sylvia served as director of strategy, plans, and policy on the Joint Staff, a key position responsible for coordinating military planning and advising the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the president. A Pentagon official accused Sylvia of leaking classified information related to the wars in Iran and Ukraine, according to CBS News, though the allegations have not been independently substantiated. Sylvia's dismissal is the latest in a series of departures involving nearly two dozen senior military leaders under Hegseth. Palestine Israeli drone strike in central Gaza kills two Palestinians: Two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded on Thursday in an Israeli targeting a vehicle near the entrance to the Maghazi refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip, according to WAFA. Israeli forces demolish homes in the occupied West Bank as Hebron siege enters seventh day: Hebron: Israel's military assault its seventh consecutive day on Thursday, with more than 780 families affected and approximately 5,000 Palestinians forcibly displaced or confined to their homes, particularly in the sealed-off neighborhoods of Al-Jalda and Deir Bahha, WAFA reported. More than 115 Palestinians have been arrested since the operation began. Israeli restrictions have disrupted in-person education for an estimated 80,000 students across the governorate, with 66 schools directly affected. On Thursday, Israeli forces arrested seven Palestinians and injured two others during raids. In Tarqumiya, northwest of Hebron, Israeli bulldozers demolished an inhabited home, leaving seven family members homeless. Salfit: Israeli forces three homes in Deir Ballut and Bruqin. In the Wadi Al-Ahmar area, Israeli settlers stole olives from Palestinian farmland that owners had been prevented from accessing. Settlers fired live ammunition toward a Palestinian farmer who encountered them. Jericho: Israeli forces agricultural structures and bulldozed farmland east of Jericho. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: Israeli settlers Palestinian olive harvesters in Kafr Malik, northeast of Ramallah. Israeli settlers beat U.S. journalist and Russian activists in West Bank: Israeli settlers attacked U.S. journalist Jasper Nathaniel and two Russian activists in the Palestinian village of Umm Al-Khair in Masafer Yatta, in the occupied West Bank, before Israeli authorities arrested two of the victims, according to Russian activist Adele Shoko. Videos by Shoko show several men, some armed, beating Nathaniel and Russian activist Andrey X. "Andrey was severely beaten and lost consciousness several times in front of police," Shoko wrote, adding that he was denied hospital treatment and taken to a police station instead. "Jasper and I were also beaten. Jasper was then pepper-sprayed and arrested." Another video showed Nathaniel shouting, "I just got beat up," as Israeli forces led him away. Health Ministry stresses urgency of increased medical evacuations through Rafah: On Thursday, the Gaza Health Ministry reiterated its call for the opening of the Rafah crossing to allow for patients requiring medical treatment to leave and to increase the number of people allowed to travel on medical evacuations. "The successive and sudden closures of the crossings, and the deliberate slowness in the procedures, have turned the file of medical transfers from a humanitarian rescue path to a fatal obstacle; which caused a serious deterioration in the health conditions of thousands of wounded and sick, and the loss of dozens of them to their lives while waiting to be allowed to travel," the ministry said in a statement. Last week, Drop Site News that the entire functioning of the Rafah crossing was in jeopardy after the UN informed Palestinian officials that, beginning in mid-November, it would stop receiving Palestinians returning from Egypt and coordinating their entry into Gaza, citing the dangers facing returnees and repeated Israeli arrests. In response to inquiries from Drop Site, UN Public Information Officer Daria Carmon responded: "At this time we are reassessing the UN facilitated return operations into Gaza through Rafah crossing. We will make a public pronouncement about our position once the review is completed later this month. The UN remains fully committed to continue supporting medical evacuation missions through Rafah Crossing." Yemen Nearly 1,700 killed and 281,000 displaced in Yemen since August: At least 1,677 people have been killed and 7,395 injured in Yemen since August amid escalating fighting, according to the World Health Organization. Between October 20 and 25 alone, the WHO recorded 559 casualties, averaging approximately 93 killed or injured per day. More than 281,000 people have been by fighting in Yemen since the beginning of August, with over half sheltering in Taiz governorate, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. Humanitarian access has deteriorated over the past three weeks after damage to a key road connecting Taiz to southern governorates forced aid deliveries onto narrow mountain routes. Three-quarters of displaced Yemenis are sheltering in sites with inadequate water, sanitation, and shelter, while more than 35,000 families lack shelter assistance and over 230,000 people need emergency water and sanitation support. In Marib, only six of 31 mobile medical teams remain operational, and 15 health facilities have shut down entirely. Ansarallah reports 101 airstrikes by Saudi-backed forces across Yemen: Ansarallah 101 airstrikes by the Saudi-led coalition across the country over the past 24 hours, including strikes targeting the Dhubab and Mocha districts near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Separately, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces said that they carried out two airstrikes on an Ansarallah military camp in the al-Ash'oub area west of Taiz. Meanwhile, air traffic at Aden International Airport resumed following a sixth Ansarallah attack on the facility, which caused casualties and damage. The National Human Rights Authority in Sana'a said on Thursday that a Saudi strike on a paint factory near the city of Taiz caused a large fire and could release toxic gases and contaminate nearby soil and groundwater. It said that the attack was a war crime. HRW: Ansarallah depriving civilians of food, medicine in Taiz: Human Rights Watch on Thursday Ansarallah, also known as the Houthis, of endangering civilians in Taiz city by enforcing a siege on hundreds of thousands of residents in the city. "Renewed efforts by the Houthis to cut off food, water, and medicine to Taizz show their utter disregard for civilian lives,", Yemen and Bahrain researcher at Human Rights Watch, said in a statement. "Throughout the 12-year-long siege of [Taiz], the Houthis have bombed, starved, and denied humanitarian aid to a million residents of the city with scant adherence to international law." An Ansarallah spokesperson told Human Rights Watch that Saudi-backed government forces were blocking roads into the city. But residents, civil society workers, and United Nations officials blamed Ansarallah for the shortages, Human Rights Watch said. Lebanon Hezbollah leader calls Israeli election results "an expression of defeat," rejects disarmament: Israel's election results were "one of the expressions of defeat," Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem said on Wednesday, pointing to what he described as Israel's internal political, economic, and social crises. "We do not concern ourselves with who governs Israel, but let it be perfectly clear that it cannot continue its occupation and must leave our land," he said, vowing to continue resistance regardless of the election outcome. Qassem insisted there was "no room for discussion" about disarming Hezbollah as long as Israel continues its occupation and attacks on Lebanon, and called for an Israeli withdrawal under the November 2024 ceasefire agreement and UN Security Council Resolution 1701. He also declared the June 26 Lebanon-Israel framework agreement "null and void." Amid concerns that Hezbollah could enter another war in support of Iran, Qassem did not clarify whether the group would intervene if the U.S. or Israel launched new attacks, but said the U.S.-Iran agreement had helped reduce Israeli attacks on Lebanon. U.S. News DoorDash buys Instacart for $17 billion: The food delivery giant Doordash on Thursday that it purchased the grocery delivery app Instacart for $17 billion, the New York Times reported. It is DoorDash's largest acquisition to date. The deal could face antitrust scrutiny and pushback from grocers and gig workers. The deal is expected to close in 2027 or 2028. DoorDash completed 993 million orders in the third quarter, up 28%, while Instacart, once valued at $39 billion by private investors, has a market capitalization of about $14 billion and relationships with more than 2,200 retailers. Dolores Huerta, labor leader and civil rights figure who co-founded United Farm Workers, dies at 96: Labor and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta on Wednesday at her home in Bakersfield, Calif., of cancer, a family spokesman said. Alongside Cesar Chavez she founded the National Farm Workers Association in 1962, and led the 1960s and '70s strikes and boycotts that helped many California grape-growers consolidate worker power. She served as the union's vice president for nearly four decades. Over her working life, police arrested her 22 times. In 1988, she was severely beaten by a San Francisco police officer--a case settled by the city for $825,000. Huerta is widely believed to have coined the phrase "Si se puede." President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012. In early 2026, she told the New York Times that Chavez raped her in 1966, and that two of her children resulted from sexual encounters with him. She is survived by 13 of her 14 children, 24 grandchildren, 23 great-grandchildren, and seven great-great-grandchildren. Fed holds rates steady: The Federal Reserve its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, with governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a quarter-point increase. The Fed rated economic activity as "strong," up from "solid." Traders see an 85% chance of a rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. Inflation has come in above target and Thursday's PCE report is expected to show a rate of 3.6% for the year through September. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said that starting next year, one of the eight annual Federal Open Market Committee meetings will focus solely on monetary policy strategy. It was Cook's first dissent, coming ahead of a White House hearing next week on Trump's bid to remove her over alleged mortgage fraud, which her lawyers call a pretext. Leak exposes records of more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors, including undercover ICE agents: The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets an archive it calls "Icepick" on Wednesday, which contains the records of more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors. In a press release, DDoSecrets said the information comes from DHS's Okta login system and was obtained by a group that calls itself the Department of Peace. That group attached a note that said, "They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs." The records, last updated on August 19, cover the DHS and seven component agencies, including emails, phone numbers, office addresses, supervisor names, and permission groups referencing undercover agents, and surveillance programs. DHS said it was working to address a potential security breach. Judge rejects Trump administration bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots: Judge David O. Carter , a Bill Clinton appointee, on Wednesday that the Trump administration's demand that California sequester 20,000 ballots "would wreak havoc and disrupt the election that is already underway" and "discount the votes of United States citizens." Carter wrote that "never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own constitutional elections procedures." He noted that the Department of Justice has filed at least 31 suits seeking state voter rolls and has won "precisely zero" of the 26 suits decided so far. He called the DOJ's effort part of "a broad, ongoing pattern of attempted election interference." The DOJ immediately appealed the ruling. DOJ turned a rights-group informant into the government 's own: The rights group Southern Poverty Law Center said one of its informants was flipped by the Trump administration, and became a government informant, according to court papers the SPLC on Wednesday. SPLC lawyers said that the informant "F-9," who worked with the group from 1996 and was paid at least $1.2 million over 16 years, has met DOJ prosecutors more than 20 times since November 2025 under immunity, exchanged about 1,800 texts with FBI and IRS agents, and given at least four "intelligence briefings" to federal authorities as part of the DOJ's ongoing fraud case against the group. One of the informant's PowerPoint presentations bore FBI and IRS seals, as though "he were an actual member of the prosecution team," the SPLC filings said. The group requested that the court order the informant to preserve all documents, and to grant a subpoena for his materials. In April, the DOJ charged the SPLC with defrauding donors, alleging that the group funneled money to informants inside white-supremacist groups. Defense lawyers said that the case began after a coalition of right-leaning groups complained to senior White House advisor Stephen Miller about the SPLC's work. Trump administration issues more than 100 subpoenas for voter records in at least 13 states ahead of midterms: Reuters more than 100 subpoenas issued by the Trump administration, mostly in the past three months, to state and local election officials. The Trump administration sought records on tens of thousands of voters. The federal government targeted Democratic strongholds like Minneapolis, Philadelphia, and Los Angeles, and Republican-leaning Texas, Kansas, and Georgia. Legal experts told Reuters that the federal government could use the records to contest close election results. One expert said that the probes are "setting up" post-election challenges. California elites spend $612 million to defeat billionaire tax: Seventy past and current California billionaires have spent a record-setting $612 million to block a one-time, 5% tax on their wealth, . That spending has pushed support for the tax below 50%, . Company linked to Darline Graham 's husband was sanctioned for arming Russia against Ukraine: Lindsey Graham's central political ambition was to confront and contain Russia. The former South Carolina senator died within hours of returning from Ukraine, where he toured a drone factory as one of his last acts on his earth. His sister Darline Graham now holds his seat and is on the ballot next week. It turns out that her husband works for a company linked to a Chinese firm sanctioned in 2024 for providing sophisticated military tech to Russia. . CNN Senate poll finds Democrats up in Michigan, Kansas, Maine, and Texas: President Trump is heading to South Carolina to stave off Republican catastrophe there, while polls show potentially competitive races in Iowa, Nebraska, Florida, Mississippi, and Arkansas. Four from CNN put Democrats on top in critical races: Michigan Abdul El-Sayed (D): 49% Mike Rogers (R): 42% Kansas Adam Hamilton (D): 49% Roger Marshall (R): 45% Maine Troy Jackson (D): 49% Susan Collins (R): 45% Texas James Talarico (D): 49% Ken Paxton (R): 43% 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Russian drone strike on Ukraine train station kills at least 14: A Russian jet-powered drone a busy train platform in Dnipro, Ukraine, on Thursday, killing at least 13 people. At least 14 others were injured in the attack, six of whom are in critical condition. Russian strikes also hit Kharkiv, damaging an educational institution, and a strike on the Rivne region killed one man. Fl avio Bolsonaro declares himself Brazil's rightful "leader" after arriving in Miami: Brazil's right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, who left Brazil in secret after losing the election to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, said in a Wednesday letter that he was the rightfully "elected president" of the country. He claimed that the Supreme court and Lula had carried out an "electoral coup" against him. He later amended the letter to say he was Brazil's "leader" and added that he "did not flee Brazil." He thanked Argentina's Javier Milei for helping him travel to the U.S., and thanked Trump for securing visas for him and his family. Pakistani court sentences human rights lawyers to 10 years in prison: A Pakistani anti-terrorism court prominent human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to 10 years in prison on Thursday. Their sentences will run concurrently with additional one-year and two-year sentences for obstructing and assaulting government servants. Mazari and her husband were accused of holding a protest in 2024 that blocked a road, and thereby endangered an international cricket team's security plans. They denied the charges, calling themselves "prisoners of conscience" targeted for their human rights work. Mazari's mother, Shireen Mazari, a former member of Imran Khan's cabinet, said that they were not allowed access to their lawyer or given key legal documents in the case. The couple had earlier been sentenced to 17 years in prison for social media posts. That sentence was suspended by Pakistan's Supreme Court--they were re-arrested for the 2024 protest on the same day. Clashes on Pakistan-Afghan border kill one: Clashes on the border of Afghanistan and Pakistan one person and injured five others, a Pakistani official said on Wednesday, accusing the Afghan Taliban of firing at civilian houses and a market in Pakistan's Waziristan region on Tuesday. He added that Pakistani forces would respond "effectively and heavily" to the attack. Afghan's Taliban government said Pakistan carried out four drone attacks on the district commissioner's office and nearby security facilities in Paktika province, and Afghan defense ministry spokesperson Sedeequllah Nasrat said Afghan forces retaliated against a nearby Pakistani military base, causing several casualties. Pakistan accuses Kabul of harboring militants who stage cross-border attacks, a charge the Afghan government denies. The conflict has killed hundreds of people this year. Drop Site's latest reporting on the clashes is available. South Korean prosecutors again seek death penalty for ex-President Yoon: South Korean prosecutors their effort to impose the death penalty on former President Yoon Suk-yeol at a Seoul High Court hearing on Thursday. Earlier this year, Yoon was convicted of leading an 2024 insurrection against the state. South Korea halted state executions in 1997, but prosecutors said that was "no reason to hesitate" in sending Yoon to his death. In January, prosecutors failed to secure a death penalty at Yoon's trial. He was sentenced to life in prison instead. Iraq PM visits Damascus: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa on Wednesday. The two reportedly discussed exporting Iraqi oil through Syrian territory, boosting bilateral trade and joint agricultural development, Iraqi News Agency reported. Since the U.S.-led war on Iran began, Iraq has exported oil through Syria. In July, Iraq and Syria signed deals to revive the Haditha-Baniyas pipeline, entrusting a Chevron-led consortium to implement the deal. North Korea fires short-range ballistic missiles into Sea of Japan: North Korea about 10 missiles into the Sea of Japan on Thursday, South Korea's Defense Ministry said. The test firings come just days after South Korea proposed military talks with North Korea over a border dispute. In September, a landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone separating North Korea and South Korea injured three South Korean soldiers, which joint South Korea-UN blamed on mines North Korea planted over a year ago. North Korea rejected the finding, and told the UN Security Council that South Korea fabricated the incident. El Salvador to send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti, increasing military presence: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime in a phone call on Wednesday that he will deploy more than 2,000 troops to Haiti. He claimed the military surge is intended to rescue four missing Salvadoran soldiers and support anti-gang operations in the country, according to El Salvador's foreign ministry. Bukele has already sent hundreds of soldiers to the area. The Haitian prime minister's office confirmed the call. Separately, Haiti's government announced it would postpone planned presidential elections until next year. The country has not held national elections since 2016, and its last president was assassinated in 2021. Presidential elections have been repeatedly postponed under transitional administrations. U.S. sanctions Rwanda defense ministry and Rwandan financial institution over the eastern Congo conflict: The U.S. Treasury Department sanctions on Rwanda's defense ministry and on the Zigama Credit and Savings Society on Wednesday. The U.S. accused the defense ministry of directing the previously sanctioned Rwanda Defense Force to deploy thousands of troops to the Democratic Republic of the Congo. And the U.S. accused Zigama, which it said is linked to Rwanda's security services, of facilitating payments to Chinese and other entities for weapons, and of moving gold from rebel-held Congo to Rwanda. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, "Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC." Rwanda denies backing the rebels, formerly AFC-M23. Hi Derek, it’s Dr.
Annie Andrews.

There’s a lot of new eyes on this campaign, so I wanted to take a second
to reintroduce myself.

I’m the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in South Carolina. But
that’s not it.

I’m also a mom of three who does school pick ups and watches Bluey before
bed. I’m a pediatrician of twenty years. In other words, I’m not your
typical politician.

In fact, this is the last thing I ever thought I’d be doing. But I knew
someone had to step up for the people of South Carolina.

Our campaign is people-powered by grassroots donors like
you, Derek. I don't
have a network of wealthy donors or billionaire friends. I don't have
decades of political favors to call in.

What I do have is twenty years of sitting across from families in some of
the scariest moments of their lives, listening to what they actually need,
and trying to help.

That's the experience I'm bringing to this race. Not a perfect political
resume. A real life, spent in service to the people in this state.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/21812?t=1002&akid=841%2E245147%2E-8AUwS ]I’m running for the U.S. Senate to fight for the families, kids, and
communities that need someone in their corner. So, if you’re ready to win
in November, split a donation between my campaign and Josh Shapiro today.

body:
We can only win this fight with your support.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, here’s an update you might’ve missed.
**FIRST:** We set a $2 million goal for our final October fundraising push.
**THEN:** We learned Elon Musk dropped $5 million into Greg Abbott’s campaign, making him Abbott’s single biggest donor this election.
**NOW:** We’re raising our end-of-month goal to $3 million so Gina’s campaign can stay competitive and beat Greg Abbott on Election Day.
Why would the richest man in the world spend millions on a race for Texas governor? Because he’s already gotten a great return on his investment. Months after Musk gave Abbott $500,000 earlier this year, Abbott handed Musk’s companies a $1.66 billion tax break.
_**That’s what this race is about: whether Texas is run for its billionaire donors or for the people who live here.**_
Abbott raised $26 million in a single month, with checks from billionaires like Musk. Gina’s campaign is powered by _more than 300,000_ grassroots supporters chipping in what they can. We can’t match Abbott dollar for dollar, but we don’t have to. We just have to reach enough voters before November 3rd.
**[Gina can’t win this fight without your support, Peter. Will you make a $5 contribution now to help us hit our new $3 million goal and power this grassroots campaign in the final days?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261029_2_ftn.XP2Sld&refcode=em20261029-2579&amount=5&t=1&akid=2579%2E299639%2EfvvCj-)**

Team Gina

_**First Hartford takes control of our neighborhoods. Then it tells Greenwich what to do with our taxes and schools. And somehow, our representatives still get to say they voted NO.**_
[](https://substack.com/redirect/62ef5521-c397-4b95-817a-ecf52d00a14f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## I Called It Before the Debate. I Raised It at the Debate. Now Look What's Happening.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..Oc4m4MQx3fmmhjM3XXhQzQVU4qn8zB1DE-yQwfyKEjo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=222653869)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=222653869&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIyNjUzODY5LCJpYXQiOjE3OTMyODc2MDIsImV4cCI6MTc5NTg3OTYwMiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.Yt7uTl7FJLXr6cbUcCOu5frPg54MC9wGNtcaxaSkg7Y)
There is a political tradition in Hartford that Greenwich residents should understand.
I call it the **Hall Pass and the Full Moon.**
**The Hall Pass:** When a controversial bill already has enough votes to pass, a legislator can vote NO, go home, and tell constituents they opposed it. But what did they actually do to stop it?
**The Full Moon:** When Hartford turns its backside on Greenwich, takes away local decision-making power, and leaves our residents dealing with the consequences.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/269daf3b-1adc-4a22-8ccd-e9635fbfef56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It's a little political humor. But the consequences aren't funny.
And I've been warning about both throughout this campaign.
## The Hall Pass: A NO Vote Doesn't Tell the Whole Story
Let's look at the legislative record.
On May 27, 2025, Greenwich State Representative Steve Meskers voted YES on House Amendment B to HB 5002, a controversial housing bill.
Later that evening, he voted NO on the amended bill.
The bill passed the House anyway, 84-67.
Those are recorded votes, not speculation.
That bill was subsequently vetoed by Governor Lamont. But the housing debate did not end there. [My father and I wrote this as a father son piece back then.](https://substack.com/redirect/8976de94-85ab-485a-846e-1e9afcc4e29d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In November 2025, Hartford enacted a different housing measure, HB 8002, which became Public Act 25-1. [We covered that too ](https://substack.com/redirect/df3e16a4-2c2f-4396-a71b-809cccc6855d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)as the father -son duo as we care about this state and built this Substack to over 23,000 people.
My criticism is not that every NO vote is meaningless. My criticism is that **a final NO vote is only part of the record.**
Did your representative challenge the bill? Debate its consequences? Offer amendments? Fight for sewer capacity, parking, local infrastructure, and municipal authority?
Or did the opposition end with a vote after the outcome was effectively decided?
I've called this a political _hall pass_. That's my characterization of a legislative practice--not a claim that anyone privately arranged a deal.
**A hall pass may get a politician off the hook. It doesn 't get Greenwich off the hook. That is where we stand in the 150th with your current representative - Just another seat at the table but no voice for Greenwich.**
## The Full Moon: Your Neighbor Sells. Hartford Changes the Rules.
Picture this.
You've lived in Greenwich for 20 or 30 years. You bought your home, raised your children, invested in your property, and chose your neighborhood for a reason.
Then your neighbor sells.
What gets built next door?
Should the answer come from Greenwich's Planning and Zoning Commission, applying local standards, or from state laws that limit what local officials can require?
Public Act 25-1 changes Connecticut's housing planning and zoning framework, including rules governing certain developments and minimum off-street parking requirements.
Not every home sale permits a large apartment building. Existing zoning and applicable legal requirements still matter. But the broader question is real: **How much authority should Greenwich retain over its own neighborhoods?**
What about traffic? Sewer capacity? Drainage? Schools? Parking?
Hartford may write the rules. Greenwich residents live with the results.
That's what I mean by the Full Moon.
**Hartford turns its backside on local concerns, and Greenwich gets the view.**
## And Now Hartford Is Looking at Your Taxes and Schools
On October 26, 2026, the CT Mirror reported that the Connecticut Citizens' Assembly on Property Taxes recommended proposals including highway tolls, a surcharge on high incomes, incentives for school regionalization, and changes to special education financing.
These are recommendations, not enacted laws. The assembly also proposed measures intended to reduce municipal burdens, including greater state support for special education.
But these recommendations raise questions that I believe Greenwich should confront now, not after legislation is drafted.
Who decides how our schools are organized?
Will local taxpayers receive genuine property tax relief, or will one set of taxes simply replace another?
Will Greenwich retain control of education and development decisions?
And will state lawmakers be willing to challenge proposals from their own leadership?
I warned that Hartford's expansion into local zoning could be followed by more debates over local fiscal and educational control.
**Now those debates are on the table.**
That is what I meant when I said I called it.
I did not predict every recommendation. I predicted the larger conflict over who controls Greenwich's future.
## Greenwich Is Not Stamford
Stamford is a city. Its density, development needs, transportation network, and municipal priorities are different.
Greenwich has different neighborhoods, infrastructure, and planning needs.
Housing affordability is a legitimate concern. So is the need to provide opportunities for younger residents, working families, and seniors.
But housing policy must account for the infrastructure necessary to support growth.
We cannot simply look at how many housing units a sewer system can accommodate in dry weather while ignoring what happens during a heavy rainstorm.
We already have concerns about sewage entering Long Island Sound and beach closures.
Development decisions and infrastructure planning belong in the same conversation.
**One size does not fit all.**
## I'd Rather Make Noise at the Kids' Table Than Sit Quietly at the Grown-Ups' Table
I've said throughout this campaign that I may be part of the minority in Hartford.
I understand that.
But I've also raised an important question: Have you ever heard how much noise kids can make at the kids' table?
Sometimes they make so much noise that the grown-ups have to stop talking and pay attention.
That's the kind of representation I'm talking about.
As an attorney, I've negotiated with people who had more leverage than I did. In construction, I know that problems don't disappear because someone refuses to acknowledge them.
You challenge the assumptions. You ask the uncomfortable questions. You demand answers. You put alternatives on the table.
And you make sure that the people making decisions cannot say nobody warned them.
**I would rather be heard from the minority table than sit quietly at the majority table.**
## No More Hall Passes. No More Full Moons.
My priorities remain simple:
**A -- Affordability:** Address outrageous utility costs, eliminate the Public Benefits Charge from electricity bills, and pursue a temporary gas and diesel tax holiday.
**B -- Beaches:** Address sewage pollution, infrastructure failures, and beach closures affecting Long Island Sound.
**C -- Local Control:** Protect Greenwich's voice in zoning, development, infrastructure, and education decisions.
**I 'm not going to Hartford to ask for a hall pass. **
I'm going to Hartford to ask questions, challenge bad bills, offer alternatives, and make sure Greenwich is heard. I may have to go up there with a hard hat and safety glasses - but that's what PPE is all about and a good pair of boots
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ae015a87-3606-4add-9443-8948fba85589?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And when Hartford gives us the Full Moon, I won't pretend the sun is shining.
**Greenwich deserves more than a representative who can say he voted NO. Greenwich deserves a representative who makes sure its concerns are heard before the vote.**
I'm Jonathan Goldstein, and I'm asking for the opportunity to represent Greenwich in Hartford.
**Not Red. Not Blue. Just Greenwich.**

Time and again, she started her answer by saying she agreed with her opponent. On the Iran war, she said “I agree that the president did not have a good plan.” She’s been in the Senate since 1997 and is asking for a sixth term, something no senator from Maine has ever won. Her opponent Troy Jackson is a fifth generation logger from Allagash and a former President of the Maine Senate. He isn’t backed by corporate PACs or billionaire donors. | | | | The very first question at that debate was how to bring down heating costs in Maine. The war has pushed heating oil and gas prices up across the state, right as winter sets in. Agreeing it was a bad plan doesn’t lower anyone’s oil bill. A New York Times analysis of her record found her votes against Trump have rarely stopped anything. _**Peter**_ , I’m going to keep this short, because it comes from the heart and those kind of things don’t need a lot of words. **We are less than a week out. In just a few days, the votes will be cas t.** I’ve been sitting here thinking about the miles we’ve put behind us to get to this point, and more than anything, thinking about you, **Peter**. You know, back home in Jackson, we’ve got a saying: You find out who’s really in your corner when the road gets tough. _**Peter**_ , you’ve been in my corner every single mile of this haul. Every dollar you’ve given, every prayer you said, you have carried me through the days when the finish line felt a long way off. I don’t have the fancy words to tell you what that means to me. I’m just a Georgia boy who drives trucks and fights hard for the people I love. name: Adam Ukman, The Dads Initiative
subject: What We Learned about Connecting with Dads this Year
body:
Some of our favorite moments from this year, and a giveaway for one lucky family.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/4ebf2177ef6d/the-dads-initiatives-second-show-cart-talk-7232753?e=7e921d898f)
---
| | | | Hi Peter,
I’m Adam, and I run The Dads Initiative at ParentsTogether. We make entertaining shows, conduct research, and drive conversations for dads trying to show up well for their families, even when nobody gave them the playbook.
As we near the end of the year, I wanted to share a few things that stuck with me in 2026:
1. **Dads really love to talk about being dads.** On Cart Talk, we put dads in a golf cart and they open up about their own fathers, the pressure to provide, and what they’d do differently. If you haven’t seen it, this episode with author [Tom](https://us.list-manage.com/QQBXF6lgIZg?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/1ICtvdB28sX?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)[Coyne](https://us.list-manage.com/Z2ou3IpE0nL?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) is a good place to start.

2. **Small habits matter.** On [Reset Mode](https://us.list-manage.com/he3o1C6Q0sD?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf), creator Sidney Raskind talks about modeling a love of reading for his kid. Kids learn more from what we do than from what we say.

3. **Dads have something to say about the world our kids deserve.** After the Cornell 7 news, hundreds of dads signed our Open Letter committing to do better as men and fathers. [You can still read and sign it](https://us.list-manage.com/lp7n2Nia5iz?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf).

---
| | **Enter our Giveaway** To celebrate the year, we’ve partnered with child furniture brand **dadada** to give one family a [toddler tower](https://us.list-manage.com/SpBTMO0KNYD?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf). As a toddler dad myself, I can tell you it’s a game changer. To enter, just [comment on this post](https://us.list-manage.com/vPYU4THt6x8?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) and follow [@ResetModeShow](https://us.list-manage.com/67vFXQaM1jA?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) and [@Dadadababyusa](https://us.list-manage.com/18TXFncAIRa?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) on Instagram by November 15.
---
| [Comment on this post to enter the giveaway](https://us.list-manage.com/1D0ibck5rL7?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)
---
| | **What’s Next
** In 2027 we’re launching new shows with creators dads already trust, and building something bigger around Father’s Day. Before then, I’d love to know: what’s a conversation about being a dad you wish more men were having? Just hit reply. I read these.
---
| | Wishing you and your family a good Thanksgiving and a restful holiday season.
AdamFounder, The Dads Initiative
P.S. Don’t forget to [enter](https://us.list-manage.com/IPp9Atj4Z6a?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) the toddler tower giveaway before November 15!

body:
We stand by our reporting.

We stand by our reporting.

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.com/click/e9772510/UaHR0cHM6Ly9vZGIubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvdmRxbUVwR0NuMw/SZW1haWxfZnJlZXRoaW5rZXJkYWlseV9jb20yNjEwMjk/LbmNsckdQdTVEbw/qP2hpZHM9bmNqa1l1dktsdFczdjBsc10/gauNzKQ/s3vbd602a9c

[O'Keefe Media Group]
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

[Statement: Minnesota charged me with two felonies. I never settle.
Stand with James.]
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Dear Patriot,

Minnesota charged both myself and fellow journalist Cam Higby with two
felony counts in retaliation for our bombshell investigative report on
voter vouching laws that we did back in August.

WE STAND BY OUR REPORTING.

I recorded a statement on these charges, and I WANT YOU TO WATCH IT
AND STAND WITH ME
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

[Watch: James O'Keefe statement on Minnesota felony charges. Watch
and stand with James.]
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

The charges are an attempt to criminalize investigative journalism.
The charges are an attempt to distract from what our reporting exposed
as insecure elections in Minnesota. Now, this has become a landmark
1st Amendment case where EVERYONE'S RIGHT TO SPEAK TRUTH TO POWER HAS
JUST BEEN PUT ON THE LINE
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty led a press conference
regarding these charges.

“Today we are charging two individuals, James O'Keefe and Cameron
Higby, with felony counts of unlawful voting and identity theft.”
— MORIARTY

She also said that Cam and I could do some local jail time for our
investigative reporting.

We received a charging document that lists two felony counts.

COUNT I
Identity Theft
Knowingly misrepresented his identity in applying for a voting ballot

COUNT II
Unlawful Voting
Knowingly misrepresented his identity in applying for a voting ballot

TWO COUNTS WITH THE EXACT SAME JUSTIFICATION BENEATH EACH COUNT.

In our report, we clearly stopped and walked out of the polling places
to avoid even touching a voting ballot.

Moriarty even said it herself. She admitted that my and Higby's intent
was to act as investigative reporters.

“A group of people were attempting to cast doubt on the state's
vouching system. I think it's pretty clear they did not intend to
vote.”
— MORIARTY

They admit we didn't vote. They charged us anyway. WATCH MY STATEMENT
AND STAND WITH ME.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Moriarty also said there is no such thing as undercover journalism
when looking into election loopholes.

“If you identify as a journalist, there is no such thing as
undercover investigation in the polling place. You have to identify
yourself as a journalist in the polling place, which they did not.”
— MORIARTY

MORIARTY IS WRONG AS A MATTER OF CONSTITUTIONAL LAW.

The 1st Amendment allows reporters to show up on Election Day and ask
questions at polling booths.

But don't take my word for it. In 2012, former Attorney General of the
United States Eric Holder went under oath in Washington, D.C.
discussing an almost identical investigation asking if the polling
official has Eric Holder's ballot at a precinct on primary day there.

“What I drew from that video was that [O'Keefe] was very careful not
to say that he was Eric Holder, not to actually get a ballot. He
didn't do the kinds of things that would have subjected him to
criminal prosecution.”
— ERIC HOLDER

In today's press conference, Moriarty points out this distinction,
too.

“So, there's a difference between intent to vote and intent to apply
for a ballot. The application of a ballot is a multi-step process. I
can't anticipate what [O'Keefe and Higby's] defense is. I'm sure we'll
hear from them.”
— MORIARTY

OUR DEFENSE IS THE SHIELD OF THE 1ST AMENDMENT TO HOLD GOVERNMENT
ACCOUNTABLE TO THE PEOPLE.

We didn't apply for a ballot; we were there talking to election
clerks, posing hypotheticals, and getting answers so that Americans
could know what was happening in the elections.

Many people in the United States did not even know about vouching for
eight, and this investigative report educated them.

By the way, we conducted training and specifically told each
journalist NEVER TO SIGN AN AFFIDAVIT, NEVER TO PROCURE A BALLOT,
NEVER TO EVEN TOUCH A BALLOT.

We even did exercises training the journalists to say “the name
is” rather than “my name is.” We were very intentional about
what we were there to do, namely was to inform the public.

Moriarty admitted that we stopped short of signing any oath or
carrying out any fraud.

“Both men stopped short of signing the oath we all sign before
receiving our ballot.”
— MORIARTY

The reporters in the room questioned Moriarty on what exactly we're
being prosecuted for.

“Does that give them a way to say that we didn't commit a crime
because we didn't take it all the way? ... Can you explain why you
think it's still a crime?”
— A REPORTER AT THE PRESS CONFERENCE

So again, what exactly are we being prosecuted for? What is this
really about?

MAKE NO MISTAKE, THIS IS ABOUT PROSECUTING THE PRESS, AND THIS ISN'T
THE FIRST TIME SOMETHING LIKE THIS HAS HAPPENED TO ME.

STAND WITH JAMES →
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

In New Orleans, LA, they falsely accused me of a felony and later
admitted there was no felony. The U.S. attorneys involved in that case
were eventually disbarred.

The federal prosecutor was so furious about this case that he
literally threw my book at me.

“You're a nasty, little, cowardly spud. You are scum! I recused from
your case!”
— PROSECUTOR JIM LETTEN

Then there was the case when the FBI came knocking at my house. Agents
stormed into my home and unlocked my phone to get access to my Signal
in order to intimidate me and to intimidate the sources that come to
me.

It was such a landmark First Amendment case that the American Civil
Liberties Union (ACLU) filed amicus, and the Reporters Committee for
Freedom of the Press came to my defense.

I have been to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, challenging the
constitutionality of Oregon's recording laws. Got a reversal there.

I went up to the 1st Circuit Court of Appeals in Massachusetts there.
We won a partial victory.

In another civil case, Shirley Teter v. O'Keefe, I won at directed
verdict. For that case, there were six pro-bono lawyers representing
the plaintiff, who stated, “We're not paid by the Hillary Clinton
campaign or by the Democratic Party or anything like that.” The
federal judge pointed out the unsolicited statement only raised
further questions, and ordered them to pay my legal fees.

I have been sued so many times and have had so many criminal threats
made against me that even the media that hates me is forced to
acknowledge that I have established legal 1st Amendment precedent
throughout the nation.

We also overturned a jury verdict against me in the D.C. Circuit Court
of Appeals last month before a panel of judges, which were appointed
by Democrats. We convinced the panel to side with the 1st Amendment,
creating a new standard for undercover journalism across the board.

It's now called the “O'KEEFE PRINCIPLE.” On publication injury
when undercover journalism is involved.

I've won these fights before. STAND WITH ME AND HELP ME WIN THIS ONE.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

The politics of fear and weaponized lawfare don't seem to work against
me. It never has. Actually, it has always backfired against the people
who come after me.

Why is that? It's because what's at issue here is not actually
political; it's fundamental.

This is about whether citizens still have a right to ask questions of

Fellow Patriot,

On Monday, I was in South Carolina, on the campaign trail with Darline Graham. I want to tell you what I saw, because this race is closer than anyone in Washington wants to admit.

It is neck and neck. Election Day is less than a week away, _**and Darline's seat could swing either way.**_

Here's what I told the folks there:
> _-> You don't want a Senate run by Chuck Schumer.
> -> You don't want Elizabeth Warren to chair the Senate Banking Committee.
> -> And you don't want Bernie Sanders setting environmental policy that kills jobs in South Carolina._
That's the radical Democrat agenda, _and it's what Annie Andrews would be voting for._

She's raised over $25 million - nearly $4 million in the last couple of weeks - from liberal donors who don't share South Carolina's values. **She built her campaign attacking Lindsey, and now her whole mission is to defeat his sister.**

Darline stands for common sense: low taxes, good jobs, and backing the police. She won't vote to put violent criminals back on the street or to let boys compete in girls' sports. She has thirty years of experience working for the people of her state, and she has a backbone.

clean_body: I just left South Carolina. This race is neck and neck, and Darline needs us now. | Fellow Patriot, On Monday, I was in South Carolina, on the campaign trail with Darline Graham. I want to tell you what I saw, because this race is closer than anyone in Washington wants to admit. It is neck and neck. Election Day is less than a week away, and Darline's seat could swing either way. Here's what I told the folks there: -> You don't want a Senate run by Chuck Schumer. -> You don't want Elizabeth Warren to chair the Senate Banking Committee. -> And you don't want Bernie Sanders setting environmental policy that kills jobs in South Carolina. That's the radical Democrat agenda, and it's what Annie Andrews would be voting for. She's raised over $25 million - nearly $4 million in the last couple of weeks - from liberal donors who don't share South Carolina's values. She built her campaign attacking Lindsey, and now her whole mission is to defeat his sister. Darline stands for common sense: low taxes, good jobs, and backing the police. She won't vote to put violent criminals back on the street or to let boys compete in girls' sports. She has thirty years of experience working for the people of her state, and she has a backbone. What Darline doesn't have is Hollywood money. Schumer needs JUST FOUR SEATS to take the majority, and he's betting South Carolina hands him one because Darline is being outspent after running two elections back-to-back. Fellow Patriot, races this close are decided in the final days by who can stay on the air, keep volunteers knocking doors, and get voters to the polls. They tried this playbook on me in Texas. National Democrats dumped millions to attack me because they thought the bigger bank account would win. Now I'm making a personal plea: show up for Darline. | | | | | | We have less than a week. Let's not sit this one out.
